P0900.title: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit/Open
P0900.description: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator that opens and closes clutch A in an automated or dual-clutch transmission. The code sets when the module detects an open circuit, so it cannot energise the actuator. Ford documents it for the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox in the Fiesta and Focus, where each dry clutch is moved by a three-phase electric motor with hall sensors; P0900 is the open-circuit check of the clutch A motor, alongside P0902 (short to ground) and P0903 (short to power). Ford program 20B23 for some 2016-2017 Focus cars lists P0900 with a lit check engine light and erratic shifts caused by failed clutch actuator motors. P090A is the same fault on clutch B.

causes.label: Failed clutch A actuator motor (open winding or internal fault)
Loose connector or broken wire between TCM and actuator
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM

symptoms: Check engine light on
Erratic or missed shifts, vibration on take-off
Transmission in limp mode, possibly no drive

P0901.title: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0901.description: Set when the clutch A actuator circuit is electrically present but does not behave as expected, for instance when the measured current or response deviates too far from the target. Usage differs by maker. Ford lists P0901 among the DPS6 PowerShift codes, and trade guidance recommends swapping the two identical clutch motors: if the fault moves to clutch B, the motor is bad. Honda added P0901 on the 2015 TLX V6 nine-speed automatic for abnormal resistance in the clutch pressure control solenoid circuits, with failsafe gear hold and MIL. FCA recall 16V529 on 9-speed models also uses it to decide on a harness replacement. P0900, P0902 and P0903 are the pure circuit faults; P090B is the clutch B counterpart.

causes.label: Weak or worn clutch A actuator motor (dual-clutch units)
High resistance in the transmission harness or sub-harness
TCM fault or outdated TCM software

symptoms: Check engine light on
Shudder, harsh engagement or missed shifts
Failsafe mode with a held gear

P0902.title: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit Low
P0902.description: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a low state, in practice a short to ground on a motor or control line. Ford defines it exactly this way for the DPS6 PowerShift transmission: the TCM tests the three-phase clutch A motor for open circuit (P0900), short to ground (P0902) and short to power (P0903), next to hall sensor and sequence checks. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P0902 among the codes for which a failed TCM can be the cause, so the module itself is a real suspect besides the motor and harness. P090C is the same fault on clutch B. With the clutch no longer controllable, the gearbox goes into a fallback mode.

causes.label: Clutch A actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Chafed motor wire touching ground

symptoms: Check engine light on
No drive or only some gears available
Jerky take-off and shift faults

P0903.title: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit High
P0903.description: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a high state, meaning a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage. Ford names P0903 as the short-to-power test of the clutch A motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox of the Fiesta and Focus, part of a set with P0900 for an open circuit and P0902 for a short to ground. Ford's OBD summary gives no thresholds for these motor checks. Because both DPS6 clutch motors are identical, swapping them shows whether the motor or the harness and TCM side is at fault. CARB requires such circuit checks on transmission output components. P090D is the same fault on clutch B. The clutch is released and the vehicle may not drive normally.

causes.label: Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Internal fault in the clutch A actuator motor
Faulty motor driver in the TCM

symptoms: Check engine light on
Limp mode, gears missing or no drive
Harsh or delayed engagement

P0904.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A
P0904.description: Circuit A of the gate select position sensor tells the control module of an automated manual gearbox where the shift mechanism stands in the select direction, i.e. which gate (for example 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 or reverse) is lined up. This generic circuit code sets when the module sees an electrical fault on that signal that is not covered by the more specific low, high or intermittent variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. Aisin AI and Isuzu patents describe such select stroke or select position sensors working next to an electric or hydraulic select actuator, and CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs of this kind. P0905 to P0908 are the siblings, P09A2 and P09A6 the same signal on circuits B and C. Without a valid gate signal the gearbox usually stops shifting or holds one gear.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector at the gate select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty gate select position sensor (often integrated in the shift and select actuator)
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops shifting or stays in one gear
Neutral indicator flashes or vehicle will not pull away

P0905.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A Range/Performance
P0905.description: Plausibility fault of the gate select position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The signal is electrically within limits, but it does not fit what the control module expects: typical checks compare the measured select travel with the learned gate positions and the commanded target gate. No manufacturer documents this code in freely citable material. Patents by Aisin AI on select control with target and actual gate, and on fallback strategies after a stroke sensor failure, show how the module depends on this signal; CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0904, P0906 and P0907 cover the electrical faults, P0909 a select movement that misses its target. The driver typically sees a fallback mode with no or limited shifting.

causes.label: Worn or drifting gate select sensor, main and redundant tracks disagree
High resistance at connector pins distorting the sensor voltage
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or TCM replacement
Loose or displaced magnet or sensor mounting on the select shaft

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox drops to neutral or refuses certain gears
Slow or jerky gear changes in fallback mode

P0906.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A Low
P0906.description: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Common causes are a short to ground on the signal line, a missing sensor supply, or an internal sensor defect; with many sensor designs a broken signal wire also reads low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Aisin AI and Isuzu describe select stroke and select position sensors with a defined voltage curve across the gates in their patents, so a value below that curve is clearly out of range; CARB calls for out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0907 is the matching high fault, P09A4 and P09A8 are the low faults of circuits B and C. Without a gate signal the gearbox usually locks gear changes or holds a safe gear.

causes.label: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gear changes possible or gearbox stays in neutral
Warning message about the transmission on the dashboard

P0907.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A High
P0907.description: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Typical causes are a short of the signal line to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, a broken sensor ground, or an internal sensor fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The patents of Aisin AI and Isuzu on select control show that the module derives the active gate directly from this sensor voltage, so a reading above the valid band leaves it blind in the select direction; CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0906 is the opposite low fault, P09A5 and P09A9 are the high faults of circuits B and C. For the driver this usually means a warning lamp and a gearbox that no longer changes gear or stays in a fallback gear.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed

P0908.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A Intermittent
P0908.description: Points to a gate select position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox, too briefly or too irregularly for a steady low or high fault. Loose terminals, a damaged harness that moves with the engine, or moisture in the connector at the shift and select actuator are the usual reasons. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. An Aisin AI patent explains why even short sensor dropouts matter: if a stroke sensor fails while driving, the controller can no longer confirm the engaged gear and must switch to a fallback strategy. CARB requires circuit and rationality checks on such inputs. P0904 to P0907 are the steady faults of the same circuit. Drivers often notice occasional neutral drops or refused shifts that vanish again.

causes.label: Loose or spread terminals at the sensor or actuator connector
Harness damage that only opens or shorts under engine movement
Moisture or corrosion in the connector near the gearbox

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional drop to neutral or refused shift
Fault often disappears after restarting the engine

P0909.title: Gate Select Control Error
P0909.description: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox commands the select actuator to a new gate, but the measured select position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits may be electrically fine; the fault lies in the closed loop as a whole. Typical reasons are a jammed or stiff select shaft or shift head, a worn or weak select motor, or a sensor offset. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. An Aisin AI patent describes select control with target and actual gates, and a Hyundai/Kia patent detects jammed or stuck shift actuators from motor current. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0910 to P0913 are the actuator circuit faults, P0919 the same error in the shift direction. The gearbox may refuse gears or stay in neutral.

causes.label: Stiff or jammed select shaft, shift head or internal selector mechanism
Worn select motor (brushes, gears) with too little force
Select sensor offset or gate positions not relearned
Weak battery or voltage drop on the actuator supply

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Certain gears cannot be engaged or gearbox stays in neutral
Clicking or whirring from the actuator without a gear change

P090A.title: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit/Open
P090A.description: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator for clutch B, the second clutch of a dual-clutch transmission, and sets when the module finds an open circuit. Ford uses it on the DPS6 PowerShift of the Fiesta and Focus: the clutch B electric motor is tested for driver faults (P087A), hall sensor faults (P087B), sequence errors (P087E), an open circuit (P090A), a short to ground (P090C) and a short to power (P090D). Trade guidance for the DPS6 is to swap the two identical clutch motors; if the code moves to the clutch A equivalent P0900, the motor is defective, otherwise the harness or TCM is. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. Shifting becomes erratic and the gearbox may refuse to drive.

causes.label: Failed clutch B actuator motor
Loose connector or broken wire to the clutch B motor
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM

symptoms: Check engine light on
Even gears or reverse missing, erratic shifts
Limp mode or no drive

P090B.title: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Performance
P090B.description: Set when the clutch B actuator circuit is electrically connected but the actuator does not respond as commanded, for example too slowly or with an unexpected current draw. Ford uses P090B on the DPS6 PowerShift transmission. Trade guidance for this gearbox starts with a visual check of the harness from the TCM to the clutch B motor, then swaps the two identical clutch motors: if the code becomes P0901, the motor with its built-in position sensor is faulty; if P090B stays, the circuit or TCM needs pinpoint testing. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P090B as a code where the TCM itself can be the cause. P090A, P090C and P090D are the pure circuit faults of clutch B.

causes.label: Worn or sluggish clutch B actuator motor
TCM fault (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Damaged harness between TCM and clutch B motor

symptoms: Check engine light on
Shudder or slipping in even gears and reverse
Delayed or missed shifts, possible limp mode

P090C.title: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Low
P090C.description: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a low state, which on the documented application means a short to ground. Ford defines P090C as the short-to-ground check of the clutch B motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox, paired with P090A for an open circuit and P090D for a short to power. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P090C among the codes that a defective TCM can cause, so the module belongs on the suspect list along with the motor and its wiring. Swapping the identical clutch motors helps: if the fault moves to P0902, the motor is bad. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. Expect missing gears, erratic shifts or no drive.

causes.label: Clutch B actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Chafed motor wire touching ground

symptoms: Check engine light on
Even gears or reverse unavailable
Limp mode or no drive

P090D.title: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit High
P090D.description: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a high state, i.e. a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage. Ford documents P090D as the short-to-power check of the clutch B motor in the DPS6 PowerShift transmission of the Fiesta and Focus. Ford customer satisfaction program 20B23, covering some 2016-2017 Focus cars, names P090D together with P0900 and several hall and driver codes as signs of failed clutch actuator motors, with erratic shifting, vibration and a lit check engine light; dealers replaced both motors. P090A and P090C are the open and ground faults of the same circuit, P0903 the clutch A equivalent. CARB requires circuit checks on such transmission outputs.

causes.label: Failed clutch B actuator motor (Ford program 20B23)
Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Faulty motor driver in the TCM

symptoms: Check engine light on
Erratic or missed shifts and vibration
Limp mode, possibly no drive

P0910.title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit/Open
P0910.description: Concerns the drive circuit of the gate select actuator, the motor or valve that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox sideways from gate to gate. The code sets when the control module finds this output open or electrically faulty, for example when no current flows although the driver stage is switched on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia patents describe select and shift actuators as electric motors fed by the transmission controller; older and heavy-duty systems use hydraulic or pneumatic select cylinders with solenoid valves. CARB requires circuit checks on such outputs. P0911 to P0913 are the range, low and high variants, P0909 a select movement that misses its target. Without the select actuator the gearbox cannot change gates and stays in its current gear or neutral.

causes.label: Open winding or worn brushes in the select motor
Broken actuator wire or terminal pushed out of the connector
Corroded actuator connector near the gearbox
Faulty actuator driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox cannot change between gates, only some gears available
Vehicle may stay in neutral and not drive off

P0911.title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P0911.description: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but the current, voltage or response measured on it does not fit the command, for example a current that is too high or too low for the requested movement. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent explains why controllers watch actuator current closely: jamming and sticking raise the motor load, and the motor can be damaged if this is not caught early. An Isuzu patent describes electric select actuators controlled by the transmission module. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0910, P0912 and P0913 are the clear electrical faults, P0909 the failure to reach a gate. Gear changes become slow or are blocked.

causes.label: Worn select motor drawing abnormal current
Stiff select mechanism overloading the actuator
High resistance in actuator wiring or connector

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slow, hesitant or aborted gear changes
Gearbox enters fallback mode with limited gears

P0912.title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit Low
P0912.description: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state, which usually means a short to ground on a motor or control line, or an internal short in the actuator. Many controllers then switch the affected output off to protect the driver stage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia describe in their patents select and shift actuators built as electric motors and driven by the transmission controller, which is the hardware this circuit check covers; CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. P0913 is the matching high fault, P0910 an open circuit and P0911 a plausibility fault. With the select actuator disabled, the gearbox can no longer change gates.

causes.label: Actuator wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the select motor, e.g. from brush debris
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gate change possible, gearbox stays in current gear or neutral
Vehicle may not pull away

P0913.title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit High
P0913.description: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Usual causes are a short of a motor or control line to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on the circuit design an open load can also read high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents by Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia describe electric select and shift actuators that the transmission controller powers directly, and CARB requires circuit checks on such outputs. P0912 is the opposite low fault, P0910 the open circuit, P0911 the plausibility fault and P0909 a select movement that misses its gate. The driver sees a warning lamp and a gearbox that can no longer change gates.

causes.label: Actuator wire shorted to battery voltage
Open motor winding read as high voltage by the driver stage
Driver stage in the transmission control module stuck on

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops changing gates or holds one gear
Actuator may run noisily or get hot

P0914.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A
P0914.description: Circuit A of the gear shift position sensor reports how far the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox has moved in the shift direction, i.e. whether a gear is engaged, in neutral or in between. This generic circuit code sets on an electrical fault on that signal that does not match the more specific variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. An Aisin AI patent pairs such a shift stroke sensor with a select stroke sensor, and a Nissan/Aichi patent places the shift position sensor as a magnet and field detector on the piston of a hydraulic shift actuator. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0915 to P0919 are the siblings, P091A and P095A the same signal on circuits B and C. Without it the module cannot confirm the engaged gear and usually blocks shifting.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector at the shift sensor or actuator unit
Damaged sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty gear shift position sensor
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops shifting or stays in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed

P0915.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Range/Performance
P0915.description: Plausibility fault of the gear shift position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The voltage stays within its electrical limits, but the reading does not fit: the signal does not change while the shift actuator moves, or the engaged position does not match the learned gear positions. No manufacturer documents this code in freely citable material. A Nissan/Aichi patent points out that sensor brackets on shift forks can deform under vibration and spoil the reading, and an Aisin AI patent describes the fallback when a stroke sensor can no longer be trusted. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0914, P0916 and P0917 are the electrical faults, P0919 a shift movement that misses its target. Shifting becomes limited or stops.

causes.label: Worn or drifting shift position sensor, redundant tracks disagree
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rod
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or TCM replacement
High resistance at connector pins distorting the signal

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox drops to neutral while driving
Gears refused or engaged only after a delay

P0916.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Low
P0916.description: Set when the gear shift position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. A short to ground on the signal line, a lost sensor supply or an internal sensor defect are the usual causes; depending on the sensor design a broken signal wire reads low as well. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In the patents of Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi the shift stroke or shift position sensor is the only feedback telling the controller whether a gear is engaged, so a missing signal stops automatic shifting. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0917 is the matching high fault, P091C and P095C are the low faults of circuits B and C. The gearbox typically locks gear changes or drops to neutral.

causes.label: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the shift position sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gear changes possible or gearbox stays in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed

P0917.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A High
P0917.description: Set when the gear shift position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. The signal line may be shorted to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, the sensor ground may be open, or the sensor itself may be faulty. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi patents show the shift stroke or shift position sensor as the feedback that confirms an engaged gear; with a reading above the valid band the controller can no longer tell neutral from an engaged gear. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0916 is the opposite low fault, P091D and P095D are the high faults of circuits B and C, P0919 a shift movement that misses its target. Shifting is usually locked.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the shift position sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Warning message about the transmission on the dashboard

P0918.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Intermittent
P0918.description: Flags a gear shift position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox. The module sees implausible steps or brief losses that are too short or too irregular for a lasting low or high fault. Typical triggers are terminals that lose contact under vibration, a chafed harness moving with the powertrain, or moisture at the actuator connector. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents from Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi show the shift stroke sensor as the feedback that confirms an engaged gear. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0914, P0916 and P0917 are the steady electrical faults of circuit A, P0915 the plausibility fault. Shifts may abort or the gearbox may briefly fall back to neutral.

causes.label: Connector at the shift sensor or actuator unit losing contact under vibration
Chafed or partially broken sensor wire near the gearbox
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Shift position sensor with an internal contact or track fault

symptoms: Warning light comes and goes
Gear changes abort now and then or the gearbox drops to neutral
Fault often appears on rough roads or in wet weather

P0919.title: Gear Shift Position Control Error
P0919.description: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox drives the shift actuator towards a gear, but the measured shift position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits can be electrically intact; the fault concerns the closed loop as a whole. Usual reasons are a stiff or jammed shift rail or synchroniser, a weak actuator, low hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units, or a sensor offset. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent detects jammed shift actuators from motor current, and an Isuzu patent controls the shift motor by stroke ranges using a shift stroke sensor. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0909 is the same error in the select direction, P0920 to P0927 the actuator circuits. Gears may not engage.

causes.label: Stiff or jammed shift rail, shift fork or synchroniser
Worn shift motor or leaking shift cylinder that no longer delivers full force
Low pressure in the hydraulic supply on hydraulically actuated units
Shift positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Gear does not engage or engages only after a delay
Gearbox remains in neutral or locks in one gear

P091A.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit B
P091A.description: Circuit B is a second channel reporting the shift position of an automated manual gearbox, for instance a redundant sensor track or a separate sensor on another shift rail. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault on that signal that matches none of the more specific B variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, and which physical sensor carries the letter B depends on the design. Patents from Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi describe shift stroke sensors as the feedback for gear engagement, an Aisin AI patent also covers the fallback when a stroke sensor fails. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P091B to P091D are the B siblings, P0914 and P095A the same signal on circuits A and C. Shifting may be restricted.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector at the shift position sensor
Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit B
Faulty shift position sensor B
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Slower or restricted gear changes in fallback mode
Gearbox may hold a gear or stay in neutral

P091B.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit B Range/Performance
P091B.description: Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit B in an automated manual gearbox. The voltage stays within its electrical limits, yet the value does not fit: it disagrees with circuit A, does not change while the shift actuator moves, or does not match the learned gear positions. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent notes that sensor mountings on shift parts can deform under vibration and falsify the reading, and an Aisin AI patent describes how the control continues when a stroke sensor is no longer trusted. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P091A, P091C and P091D are the electrical faults of circuit B, P0915 the same check on circuit A. Gear changes may be limited.

causes.label: Worn or drifting shift position sensor, channels A and B disagree
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Harsh or aborted gear changes
Fallback mode with fewer available gears

P091C.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit B Low
P091C.description: Set when the shift position signal on circuit B of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Usually the signal line is shorted to ground, the sensor supply is missing, or the sensor has failed internally. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents from Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi present the shift stroke or shift position sensor as the feedback that confirms an engaged gear; with a reading below the valid band that confirmation is lost on this channel. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P091D is the opposite high fault, P0916 and P095C are the low faults of circuits A and C, P091B the plausibility fault of circuit B. The gearbox may run in fallback mode.

causes.label: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to ground
Open or shorted sensor supply line
Faulty shift position sensor B

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Restricted gear changes or a held gear
Engine start may be blocked if neutral cannot be confirmed

P091D.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit B High
P091D.description: Set when the shift position signal on circuit B of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. The signal line may be shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage, the sensor ground may be open, or the sensor may be faulty. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents from Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi present the shift stroke or shift position sensor as the feedback for gear engagement, so a reading above the valid band leaves the module unable to judge this channel. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P091C is the opposite low fault, P0917 and P095D are the high faults of circuits A and C, P091B the plausibility fault of circuit B. Shifting is usually restricted.

causes.label: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground
Faulty shift position sensor B

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Restricted gear changes or a held gear
Engine start may be blocked if neutral cannot be confirmed

P0920.title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit/Open
P0920.description: Concerns the drive circuit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox in the forward shift direction. Depending on design this is one of two solenoid valves on a double-acting shift cylinder or one rotation direction of an electric shift motor. The code sets when the module finds this output open or electrically faulty, e.g. no current while the driver is on. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. A ZF patent feeds each chamber of a double-acting cylinder through its own 3/2 solenoid valve, an Isuzu patent turns the shift motor forward or reverse by shift direction. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0921 to P0923 are the siblings, P0924 the reverse direction. Gears in this direction can no longer be engaged.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the shift actuator or valve
Broken drive wire between module and actuator
Open solenoid coil or motor winding in the actuator
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Some gears cannot be selected, the gearbox skips them or stays in neutral
Vehicle may only move off in a limited set of gears

P0921.title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P0921.description: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current, voltage or the resulting movement do not fit the command, for example a current that is too high for the requested stroke or a shift position that hardly changes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent explains that jamming raises the motor load of a shift actuator and must be caught early, and a ZF patent shows double-acting shift cylinders with one solenoid valve per chamber. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0920, P0922 and P0923 are the clear electrical faults, P0925 the reverse direction, P0919 the missed target. Forward shifts become slow or fail.

causes.label: Sticking shift valve, worn shift motor or stiff shift linkage
Solenoid or motor resistance out of specification
Increased contact resistance in connector or wiring
Insufficient hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Slow, harsh or aborted gear changes in one direction
Fallback mode with fewer available gears

P0922.title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit Low
P0922.description: Set when the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state. This usually points to a short to ground on a valve or motor line, or to an internal short in the actuator. Many controllers then switch the output off to protect the driver stage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A ZF patent drives each chamber of a double-acting shift cylinder through its own solenoid valve, and an Isuzu patent runs an electric shift motor in both directions, so a fault can affect one shift direction only. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0923 is the opposite high fault, P0920 the open circuit, P0926 the reverse direction. Gears in this direction are blocked.

causes.label: Drive wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil or shift motor
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the connector

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Certain gears can no longer be engaged
Gearbox may stay in neutral or hold one gear

P0923.title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit High
P0923.description: Set when the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Typical reasons are a valve or motor line shorted to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on circuit design an open load can also read high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A ZF patent describes double-acting shift cylinders whose chambers each have a 3/2 solenoid valve, and an Isuzu patent drives a shift motor forward or reverse by shift direction. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0922 is the opposite low fault, P0920 the open circuit, P0927 the reverse direction. An actuator that stays energised can hold or force a gear, so shifting is usually locked.

causes.label: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Driver stage in the control module stuck on
Open coil or winding read as high on some circuit designs

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Gearbox locks in one gear or refuses to shift
Possible grinding when a gear is pushed unintentionally

P0924.title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit/Open
P0924.description: Concerns the drive circuit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox in the reverse shift direction, i.e. opposite to the forward actuator. It does not mean the reverse gear itself. Depending on design this is the second solenoid valve of a double-acting shift cylinder or the second rotation direction of an electric shift motor. The code sets when the module finds this output open or electrically faulty. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. A ZF patent assigns one 3/2 solenoid valve to each cylinder chamber, an Isuzu patent reverses the shift motor depending on shift direction. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0925 to P0927 are the siblings, P0920 the forward direction. Gears in this direction cannot be engaged.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the shift actuator or valve
Broken drive wire between module and actuator
Open solenoid coil or motor winding in the actuator
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Some gears cannot be selected or the gearbox stays in neutral
Gear changes out of the current gear may fail

P0925.title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P0925.description: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox, the actuator that moves the shift mechanism opposite to the forward direction. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current, voltage or the resulting shift movement do not match the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent detects jammed shift actuators from rising motor current, and a ZF patent shows double-acting shift cylinders with one solenoid valve per chamber, so each direction can be judged on its own. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0924, P0926 and P0927 are the clear electrical faults, P0921 the forward direction, P0919 the missed target. Shifts in this direction become slow or fail.

causes.label: Sticking shift valve, worn shift motor or stiff shift linkage
Solenoid or motor resistance out of specification
Increased contact resistance in connector or wiring
Insufficient hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Slow, harsh or aborted gear changes in one direction
Fallback mode with fewer available gears

P0926.title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit Low
P0926.description: Set when the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox, the one moving the shift mechanism opposite to the forward direction, shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state. This usually means a valve or motor line shorted to ground or an internal short in the actuator; the module often switches the output off to protect itself. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A ZF patent drives each chamber of a double-acting shift cylinder through its own solenoid valve, an Isuzu patent runs the shift motor in both directions. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0927 is the opposite high fault, P0924 the open circuit, P0922 the forward direction. Gears in this direction are blocked.

causes.label: Drive wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil or shift motor
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the connector

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Certain gears can no longer be engaged
Gearbox may stay in neutral or hold one gear

P0927.title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit High
P0927.description: Set when the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Common reasons are a valve or motor line shorted to battery voltage or a driver stage that no longer switches off; on some circuit designs an open load also reads high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A ZF patent describes double-acting shift cylinders with a 3/2 solenoid valve on each chamber, and an Isuzu patent reverses an electric shift motor according to shift direction, so the reverse direction has its own output. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0926 is the opposite low fault, P0924 the open circuit, P0923 the forward direction. A permanently energised actuator can force a gear, so shifting is usually locked.

causes.label: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Driver stage in the control module stuck on
Open coil or winding read as high on some circuit designs

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Gearbox locks in one gear or refuses to shift
Possible grinding when a gear is pushed unintentionally

P0928.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A/Open
P0928.description: The module that drives the shift lock (brake transmission shift interlock, BTSI) sees no continuity on control circuit A, so it cannot reliably release the selector from Park. FCA/Chrysler uses the code as P0928-00 BTSI Control: bulletin 08-072-14 (2013-14 Ram 1500, 2014 Durango with 8-speed) and 21-034-15 (2015 Chrysler 300 rotary shifter) name it when the selector will not leave Park or the knob turns without the brake applied; the cure there is a new electronic shifter. P0929 is the plausibility fault, P0930 and P0931 the low and high faults of circuit A, P092A the same open fault on circuit B. The driver usually cannot shift out of Park until the fault clears or the manual release is used.

causes.label: Internal fault in the electronic shifter module, often logged together with P0607 (documented by FCA)
Shift lock solenoid coil open
Broken wire, poorly crimped or pushed-out terminal on the shift lock circuit

symptoms: Selector lever will not move out of Park even with the brake pressed
Problem may disappear after the ignition is switched off and the modules go to sleep
Rotary or electronic shifter can be moved without the brake applied
Shift position flashes or a message asks to return the selector to Park

P0929.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P0929.description: Set when the shift lock actuator on circuit A is electrically present but does not respond as commanded, for example it fails to reach the locked or released position. Ford stores it in the gear shift module (GSM): SSM 51057 and 53039 list P0929:77 (commanded position not reachable) on Mach-E, Escape, Bronco Sport, Maverick and Transit, fixed by GSM software or replacement; TSB 25-2045 adds P0929:00, :07 and :9A on 2021-24 F-150 together with a selector that will not leave or enter Park, and checks pin 3 of connector C211. Ford shows the wrench lamp, not the MIL. P0928, P0930 and P0931 are the pure electrical faults of circuit A, P092B the same fault on circuit B.

causes.label: Gear shift module software that misjudges the actuator position (Ford reprogramming bulletins)
Worn or binding lock actuator inside the shifter assembly
Poor pin fit or damaged pin at the shifter connector

symptoms: Wrench or transmission warning lamp on
Selector will not leave Park or will not go back into Park
Clicking from the shifter or a selector that does not stow or unstow

P092A.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B/Open
P092A.description: Reports an open on control circuit B of the shift lock. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none says which lock is B. One possible use is a second lock actuator: GHSP patents describe shifters where a further solenoid holds the lever in Neutral below a set speed unless the brake is pressed, beside the usual Park lock. CARB requires output circuits to be checked for continuity but may exempt safety-only systems. The FCA recall on the BTSI solenoid shows how such a lock fails in practice. P0928 is the same open fault on circuit A, P092B the plausibility fault, P092C and P092D the low and high faults of circuit B. Expect a lever that is locked in a position or no longer locked.

causes.label: Broken wire or loose terminal on circuit B at the shifter
Open coil in the second lock solenoid
Shifter connector not fully seated after console work

symptoms: Selector lever locked in one position although the brake is pressed
Lock no longer engages, lever moves freely without brake
Warning message about the shifter or transmission

P092B.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P092B.description: Set when the actuator on shift lock circuit B is wired correctly but does not reach or report the commanded lock or release state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest documented case is Ford P0929 on circuit A, where the gear shift module logs that the commanded position was not reached and the cure is new GSM software or a new module. CARB asks for a functional check of output components where feasible. GHSP patents show that a shifter can carry a second lock solenoid, for instance a Neutral lock. P092A, P092C and P092D are the open, low and high faults of circuit B, P0929 the matching fault on circuit A. The lever may stay locked, or the lock may engage late.

causes.label: Lock pin or actuator binding inside the shifter assembly
Shifter module software misjudging the actuator response
Weak battery or poor supply leaving the solenoid too little force

symptoms: Lever releases late or only after several tries
Lever stays locked in one position
Transmission or wrench warning lamp on

P092C.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B Low
P092C.description: The voltage on shift lock control circuit B is lower than expected, usually because the wire or the solenoid has a path to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly or names the lock behind circuit B. GHSP patents describe shifters with a second solenoid next to the Park lock, for example one that holds the lever in Neutral unless speed is low and the brake is applied. CARB requires output circuits to be checked for shorts but allows safety-only systems to be left out. P092D is the high fault, P092A the open and P092B the plausibility fault of circuit B; P0930 is the low fault on circuit A. A shorted lock circuit can leave the lever locked or let it move without the brake.

causes.label: Circuit B wire chafed to ground near the shifter
Shorted turns in the second lock solenoid
Liquid spilled into the shifter causing leakage to ground

symptoms: Lever locked in a position despite brake applied
Lock does not engage, lever moves without brake
Warning message about the shifter

P092D.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B High
P092D.description: The module sees a higher voltage on shift lock circuit B than the commanded state allows, such as a short to supply or, with a low-side driver, an open coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The documented counterpart on circuit A is FCA P0931 in recall 16V-249, where a badly crimped BTSI solenoid terminal on 2016 Grand Cherokees set the high fault and kept the lever in Park. GHSP patents show that a shifter may carry a second lock solenoid, so circuit B can be a separate lock. CARB requires circuit fault checks on outputs, with an exemption path for safety-only systems. P092C is the low, P092A the open fault of circuit B; P0931 is the same fault on circuit A.

causes.label: Circuit B wire shorted to a supply voltage
Poor crimp or loose terminal at the second lock solenoid
Open coil in the second lock solenoid

symptoms: Lever will not release from its locked position
Fault appears intermittently with vibration
Warning message about the shifter or transmission

P0930.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A Low
P0930.description: The voltage on control circuit A of the shift lock solenoid stays below the expected level, typically a short to ground or a driver output pulled low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. FCA uses the sibling codes on the same brake transmission shift interlock (P0928 BTSI Control, P0931 on the 2016 Grand Cherokee). CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit continuity and shorts, while a safety-only system may be exempt, which is why these faults often do not light the MIL. P0928 is the open, P0931 the high fault, P0929 the plausibility fault of circuit A; P092C is the low fault on circuit B. Depending on the design the selector stays locked in Park or is no longer locked at all.

causes.label: Shift lock control wire chafed through to ground in the console or under the carpet
Shorted turns in the shift lock solenoid coil
Spilled liquid in the shifter area causing leakage to ground

symptoms: Selector lever stuck in Park although the brake is pressed
Selector can be moved out of Park without pressing the brake
Shift lock override slot needed to move the lever

P0931.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A High
P0931.description: The control module reads a voltage on shift lock circuit A that is higher than the commanded state allows. FCA documents the code directly: in recall 16V-249 the Jefferson North plant found 2016 Jeep Grand Cherokee (WK) vehicles with active or stored P0931-00 whose selector would not release from Park. The cause was a badly crimped terminal on the BTSI solenoid harness from shifter supplier GHSP; FCA replaced the gear selector and warned that losing the solenoid could leave the lever locked in Park or Neutral. So a poor connection, not only a short to battery, can show up as High. P0930 is the low, P0928 the open fault of circuit A; P092D is the high fault on circuit B.

causes.label: Poorly crimped or loose terminal on the shift lock solenoid harness (FCA recall 16V-249)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open shift lock solenoid coil seen as high voltage by a low-side driver

symptoms: Selector lever will not release from Park
Lever may lock in Park or Neutral unexpectedly after stopping
Fault comes and goes with vibration or temperature

P0932.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0932.description: General electrical fault in the circuit of the sensor that reports hydraulic pressure in the gearbox, usually line pressure in an automatic or system pressure in an automated manual or dual-clutch unit. The module sees a signal it cannot use at all, without a clear low or high pattern. Chrysler names it Line Pressure Sensor Circuit Fault; an ALLDATA case on a 2003 Grand Cherokee 4.7 automatic shows it together with P0935, caused by an open line pressure solenoid in the solenoid pack. CARB requires circuit checks on such transmission inputs. P0934 and P0935 are the low and high faults, P0933 the plausibility fault, P0936 the intermittent one. Expect harsh shifts, often with line pressure forced to maximum.

causes.label: Fault in the solenoid pack or valve body module that carries the pressure sensor (open solenoid, internal lead frame)
Poor crimp or solder joint at the sensor connector terminals
5 V reference or sensor ground interrupted
Transmission or powertrain control module fault

symptoms: Warning light or transmission warning on
Harsh engagements and firm shifts from maximum line pressure
Possible limp mode with limited gears

P0933.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0933.description: The pressure reading is electrically valid but does not fit the operating state. Chrysler RFE, RLE and TES transmissions set it when measured line pressure is more than 25 psi (172 kPa) above the commanded value while staying below the highest pressure ever used in that gear; Sonnax notes that a maximum-pressure condition from an open pressure control solenoid circuit can trigger it and mislead toward the sensor. Ferrari lists P0933 on its DCT as an invalid hydraulic pressure sensor signal, read in the NCR gearbox ECU. Neighbours: P0932, P0934 and P0935 are circuit faults, P0936 intermittent, P0869 a true high line pressure. The driver notices firm or harsh shifts.

causes.label: Open circuit or fault in the line pressure control solenoid causing real excess pressure
Pressure sensor drifting or reading offset
Worn or sticking valves in the valve body
Wrong fluid level or degraded fluid

symptoms: Harsh or firm engagements and shifts
Warning light on
Shift quality does not adapt and may stay rough

P0934.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0934.description: The pressure sensor signal sits below its valid window. Chrysler RFE transmissions feed the line pressure sensor with a 5 V reference and expect 0.35 to 4.75 V; P0934 sets when the signal stays at or below 0.35 V for 0.18 s, monitored continuously with the engine running. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost 5 V reference or a failed sensor. Ferrari also uses P0934 on its DCT, described as hydraulic pressure sensor signal too low. P0935 is the opposite high fault, P0932 the general circuit fault, P0933 plausibility and P0936 intermittent. Without a usable pressure signal the control usually raises pressure to a safe maximum, so shifts turn harsh.

causes.label: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
5 V reference open or shorted
Pressure sensor or the solenoid pack carrying it failed
Control module fault

symptoms: Warning light on
Harsh shifts due to default maximum pressure
Possible limp mode

P0935.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0935.description: The pressure sensor signal sits above its valid window. On Chrysler RFE transmissions the line pressure sensor normally reads between 0.35 and 4.75 V; P0935 sets when the signal stays at or above 4.75 V for 0.18 s with the engine running. That pattern points to a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage, an open sensor ground or a sensor failed internally. An ALLDATA case on a 2003 Grand Cherokee logged it with P0932. Ferrari lists P0935 on its DCT as hydraulic pressure sensor signal too high. P0934 is the low counterpart, P0932 the general circuit fault, P0933 plausibility, P0936 intermittent. Expect harsh shifts and possibly a limp mode.

causes.label: Sensor ground open or poor terminal contact
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Pressure sensor or solenoid pack failed internally
Control module fault

symptoms: Warning light on
Harsh shifts and engagements
Possible limp mode

P0936.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0936.description: The hydraulic pressure signal drops out or jumps for short periods, too briefly or irregularly for a lasting low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The underlying sensor is the same one Chrysler uses for line pressure on RFE units and Ferrari for system pressure on its DCT, where the steady faults appear as P0934 and P0935. Gears Magazine names poor solder joints and crimps at the sensor terminals as a frequent source of intermittent pressure sensor codes. CARB requires circuit checks on such transmission inputs. P0932 to P0935 cover the general, plausibility, low and high faults. The driver may see a warning that comes and goes and occasional harsh shifts.

causes.label: Poor crimp or solder joint at the sensor connector
Chafed harness making intermittent contact
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Sensor with an internal intermittent fault

symptoms: Warning light comes and goes
Occasional harsh or erratic shifts

P0937.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0937.description: General electrical fault in the circuit of the temperature sensor for the hydraulic fluid of an automated gearbox, without a clear low or high pattern. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Ferrari shows where such a sensor sits: its DCT carries a radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor reported under P0938 to P0940 in the NCR gearbox ECU. The control needs this value to correct pressure and clutch fill for viscosity. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission sensors. P0938 is the plausibility fault, P0939 and P0940 low and high, P0941 intermittent; P0711 to P0713 cover the main transmission fluid temperature sensor. Shift quality may suffer and a warning appears.

causes.label: Connector at the temperature sensor loose, corroded or oil-soaked
Damaged sensor wiring near the gearbox or cooler lines
Temperature sensor failed

symptoms: Gearbox warning light on
Rougher shifts or clutch engagement, especially when cold

P0938.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P0938.description: By J2012 wording the hydraulic oil temperature reading is electrically valid but implausible, for example frozen, rising too slowly after a cold start or disagreeing with other temperature values. Ferrari uses P0938 on its DCT for the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor, but describes it in its bulletin as no signal, an electrical fault rather than a plausibility check; the code is read in the NCR gearbox ECU. CARB asks for rationality checks on temperature inputs. P0937 is the general circuit fault, P0939 and P0940 the low and high faults, P0941 intermittent. A wrong temperature value leads to poorly matched clutch and shift pressures and may limit the cooling strategy.

causes.label: Temperature sensor drifting or reacting sluggishly
Signal lost through connector or wiring fault (as in Ferrari's no-signal case)
Real temperature anomaly from a cooler or thermostat fault

symptoms: Gearbox warning light on
Shift and clutch quality inconsistent with operating temperature

P0939.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0939.description: The hydraulic oil temperature sensor signal sits below its valid window. With the usual NTC thermistor, a low voltage corresponds to an implausibly hot reading and typically comes from a signal wire shorted to ground or a sensor shorted internally. Ferrari uses P0939 on its DCT for the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor, described as signal too low and read in the NCR gearbox ECU. CARB requires out-of-range checks on transmission sensors. P0940 is the high counterpart, P0937 the general circuit fault, P0938 plausibility and P0941 intermittent. Because the module believes the oil is very hot, it may reduce torque, change shift strategy or show an overheat warning.

causes.label: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Temperature sensor shorted internally
Control module input fault

symptoms: Gearbox warning or overheat message
Reduced performance or altered shift behaviour

P093A.title: Hydraulic Accumulator Solenoid Circuit/Open
P093A.description: The control circuit of the solenoid that opens or locks a hydraulic accumulator in the gearbox is open. Such accumulators store pressurised fluid, for example to keep clutches applied during engine stop-start, as GM's patents on a stop-start accumulator and an accumulator with solenoid valve describe. No manufacturer documents P093A publicly. GM uses its own P171A for the same fault on the surge accumulator solenoid: failed if circuit impedance exceeds 200 kOhm in 32 of 40 samples, Type B with MIL after two trips. P093B and P093C are the low and high faults, P093D the performance fault. Stop-start is usually disabled, and the first restart may engage with a jolt.

causes.label: Accumulator solenoid coil open
Connector unplugged or wire broken between module and solenoid
Fault in the internal transmission harness or lead frame
Output driver in the control module failed

symptoms: Warning light on (after repeated detection)
Engine stop-start no longer active
Jolt or slip when driving off after an engine restart

P093B.title: Hydraulic Accumulator Solenoid Circuit Low
P093B.description: The control circuit of the hydraulic accumulator solenoid reads low, usually a control wire shorted to ground or a coil with very low resistance. No manufacturer documents P093B publicly. GM covers the same fault on its surge accumulator solenoid with P171B: failed short to ground when circuit impedance drops below 0.5 Ohm in 32 of 40 samples, Type B with MIL after two trips. The accumulator holds pressurised fluid so clutches stay applied during an engine auto-stop, as GM's stop-start accumulator patent explains. P093A is the open-circuit fault, P093C the high fault and P093D the performance fault. A grounded control line can leave the valve permanently energised, and stop-start is typically switched off.

causes.label: Solenoid control wire shorted to ground
Solenoid coil shorted internally
Output driver in the control module failed

symptoms: Warning light on (after repeated detection)
Engine stop-start no longer active
Harsh engagement after restart

P093C.title: Hydraulic Accumulator Solenoid Circuit High
P093C.description: The control circuit of the hydraulic accumulator solenoid reads high, typically a control wire shorted to battery voltage so the driver cannot switch the valve as commanded. No manufacturer documents P093C publicly. GM covers the same fault on its surge accumulator solenoid with P171C: failed short to voltage when the circuit impedance criterion of 0.5 Ohm is met in 6 of 8 samples, Type B with MIL after two trips. GM's patent on an accumulator with solenoid valve shows how the valve holds or releases the stored fluid. P093A is the open circuit, P093B the low fault and P093D the performance fault. Stop-start is usually disabled; a valve that never closes cannot keep the accumulator charged during an auto-stop.

causes.label: Solenoid control wire shorted to battery voltage
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Output driver in the control module failed

symptoms: Warning light on (after repeated detection)
Engine stop-start no longer active
Jolt when pulling away after a restart

P093D.title: Hydraulic Accumulator Solenoid Performance
P093D.description: The accumulator solenoid circuit is electrically sound, but the accumulator system does not deliver the expected hydraulic result. No manufacturer documents P093D publicly. GM's comparable P171D on the 9-speed transmission watches turbine speed during an engine auto-start: if it exceeds a predicted value because holding clutches slip from too little stored pressure, it counts a failure, enabled between 0 and 110 °C transmission fluid temperature, Type B. Gears Magazine names a solenoid stuck open or closed, a leaking accumulator piston, clutch or valve body leakage and misplaced check balls as causes. P093A to P093C are the electrical faults. Stop-start is disabled and the restart may feel like a bang.

causes.label: Accumulator solenoid stuck open (drains) or closed (no fill)
Accumulator piston or bore leaking
Leakage at clutch seals or a worn valve body
Missing or misplaced check ball after a rebuild

symptoms: Engine stop-start disabled
Lurch or bang when the engine restarts
Firm shifts with adaptive learning frozen

P0940.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0940.description: The hydraulic oil temperature sensor signal sits above its valid window. With an NTC thermistor this matches an extremely cold reading, typically from an open circuit, an unplugged connector, a broken ground or a short to a voltage source. Ferrari uses P0940 on its DCT for the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor, described as an electrical fault with signal too high, read in the NCR gearbox ECU. CARB requires out-of-range checks on transmission sensors. P0939 is the low counterpart, P0937 the general circuit fault, P0938 plausibility and P0941 intermittent. With a substitute value the gearbox works on, but clutch and shift pressures are no longer matched to the real oil temperature.

causes.label: Open signal or ground wire, or connector unplugged
Temperature sensor open internally
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

symptoms: Gearbox warning light on
Shifts or clutch engagements feel rough once warm

P0941.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0941.description: The hydraulic oil temperature signal jumps or drops out briefly, too short or irregular for a lasting low or high fault. Since fluid temperature changes slowly, a sudden step is a clear sign of an electrical problem rather than a real temperature change. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ferrari's DCT bulletin shows the related sensor at the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet, with its steady faults under P0938 to P0940. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission sensors. P0937 is the general circuit fault, P0938 plausibility, P0939 and P0940 low and high. For the driver this means a warning that may come and go and shift quality that changes from one moment to the next.

causes.label: Loose contact at the sensor connector under vibration or heat
Chafed wiring near hot gearbox or cooler parts
Sensor with an intermittent internal fault

symptoms: Warning light comes and goes
Shift quality varies unpredictably

P0942.title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit
P0942.description: General fault of the unit that generates and stores hydraulic pressure for an automated gearbox or its auxiliary oil supply: motor-driven pump, accumulator and pressure control. Toyota sets P0942 on the 2001 to 2005 MR2 Spyder sequential gearbox together with the SMT warning light and a buzzing pump, or with gears that can no longer be changed; fluid seeping from the reservoir cap or the seal of the hydraulic power unit is a known cause, fixed with new seal rings. Ferrari reads P0942 on its DCT differently, as system pressure command signal too low. CARB requires functional checks of transmission outputs. P0943 and P0944 are the cycling and pressure-loss faults, P0945 to P0948 the pump control circuit.

causes.label: Fluid loss at the reservoir cap or hydraulic power unit seals
Worn pump motor or faulty pump relay
Damaged wiring, connectors or power supply of the pump
Transmission control module fault

symptoms: Transmission or gearbox warning light on
Pump buzzing or running for long periods
Gears cannot be changed or shifts are delayed
Auto stop-start disabled or engine restarts immediately

P0943.title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Cycling Period Too Short
P0943.description: In a hydraulic pressure unit the pump charges an accumulator up to a cut-out pressure and switches off until pressure falls to the cut-in point. By J2012 wording this code means the pump switches on again too soon, so the interval between charging cycles is shorter than expected. Typical reasons are internal leakage across valves or seals, or an accumulator that has lost its gas precharge and stores too little oil. Audi patents describe such accumulator and leakage checks based on charging switch-over times and pressure decay. No manufacturer documents this exact meaning publicly; Ferrari uses P0943 on its DCT for a system pressure command signal that is too high. CARB requires functional checks of transmission outputs. P0942 is the general fault, P0944 the loss of pressure.

causes.label: Accumulator has lost its gas precharge
Internal leakage at valves, seals or actuator cylinders
Faulty pressure switch or pressure sensor giving wrong cut-in point
Low or aerated hydraulic fluid

symptoms: Pump can be heard switching on unusually often
Warning light on
Slower or harsher gear changes

P0944.title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Loss of Pressure
P0944.description: The pump runs but the expected hydraulic pressure does not build or collapses. Stellantis names it Loss of Hydraulic Pump Prime: a 2023 STAR case lists it with P0868 and a slow engagement after the vehicle has stood, both set as the only transmission codes with the MIL on, and the fix was a new transmission; an FCA defect file from 2015 also shows it beside line pressure low. Mercedes uses P0944 on the 722.9 automatic with electric auxiliary oil pump for stop-start, as internal fault of that pump; stop-start stops working, and a leaking check valve between converter housing and pump is one cause. Ferrari reads it on its DCT as no system pressure signal with pressure loss. P0943 covers short cycles, P0868 low fluid pressure.

causes.label: Pump loses prime (air drawn in through filter, seal or strainer pipe)
Blocked oil strainer or suction tube
Worn or failed pump (mechanical or electric)
Leaking check valve or internal leak in the valve body

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slow engagement after the vehicle has been parked
Auto stop-start not available or engine restarts at once
Slipping, no drive or limp mode

P0945.title: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit/Open
P0945.description: The control module drives the motor of the hydraulic pump through a relay or a direct output. This code reports a general circuit fault or an open in that control path, so the pump cannot be switched reliably. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The layout is shown by a ZF patent for an automated gearbox, in which a motor-driven pump draws oil from a reservoir and charges a pressure accumulator behind a one-way valve, with shut-off valves feeding the shift cylinders. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0946 is the plausibility fault, P0947 and P0948 low and high; P094E covers the pump supply instead of the control side. Without the pump the gearbox soon runs out of pressure.

causes.label: Pump relay coil open or relay not seated
Open control wire or loose terminal between module and relay
Failed output stage in the control module

symptoms: Warning light on
Pump does not run, pressure is not built
Gears cannot be changed or auto stop-start disabled

P0946.title: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0946.description: The pump control circuit is electrically intact, but its behaviour does not match the command, for example a pump that keeps running after being switched off, or one that switches but is not followed by the expected feedback. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. In the hydraulic unit of an automated gearbox, as shown in a ZF patent, the pump only has to run until the accumulator is charged; a relay that sticks or switches late upsets that cycle. CARB requires functional checks on transmission outputs. P0945 is the general circuit or open fault, P0947 and P0948 the low and high faults, P094B a pump stuck on regardless of the relay. A pump that never stops drains the battery and wears quickly.

causes.label: Relay contacts welded or sticking
Pump supply or control wire shorted to battery voltage
Faulty pump state feedback or control module

symptoms: Pump keeps running after switch-off
Warning light on
Auto stop-start not available
Battery discharged after parking

P0947.title: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit Low
P0947.description: The voltage on the control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver is lower than the module expects for the commanded state. Usually the line is shorted to ground or the relay coil is shorted, so the output may be overloaded and the pump runs when it should not, or the driver shuts down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The hydraulic unit it belongs to, a motor-driven pump that charges an accumulator for the shift and clutch cylinders of an automated gearbox, is described in a ZF patent. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0948 is the high counterpart, P0945 the open fault, P0946 plausibility. Pressure supply for shifting may fail.

causes.label: Relay control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Shorted relay coil
Damaged output stage in the control module

symptoms: Warning light on
Pump runs continuously or not at all
Gearbox in limp mode or stop-start disabled

P0948.title: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit High
P0948.description: The control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver shows a higher voltage than expected, typically because it is shorted to battery voltage or the relay coil is open on a low-side driver. The pump then cannot be switched on, or the module sees it as active when it is not. J2012 places this code with the pump control circuit; Ferrari however reads P0948 on its DCT as no signal from the system pressure output, an unrelated use. The pump and accumulator unit of an automated gearbox is described in a ZF patent. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0947 is the low counterpart, P0945 the open fault and P0946 the plausibility fault. Expect a warning and possible loss of pump pressure.

causes.label: Relay control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open relay coil seen as high level by the driver
Control module fault

symptoms: Warning light on
Pump does not start
Gear changes not possible or stop-start disabled

P0949.title: Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning Not Complete
P0949.description: Status code for an automatically shifted manual gearbox: the control unit has not yet finished learning its adaptation values, above all the clutch touch point and the end positions of the shift actuators. Such learning runs after a new control unit, clutch or actuator, after a software update and sometimes after the battery was disconnected; Hyundai and Kia patents show how the touch point is found and corrected from shaft speed changes. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The code is a reminder rather than a hardware fault; launch and shifts may be jerky until learning is done. P0950 to P0954 cover the manual control circuit, P0806 to P0808 the clutch position sensor. MIL use depends on the maker.

causes.label: Relearn not run after clutch, actuator or control unit replacement
Adaptation values erased by software update or battery disconnection
Learning aborted by low voltage or worn clutch outside the learn window

symptoms: Jerky launch or rough shifts
Gearbox warning or message to perform teach-in
Restricted gear selection until learning completes

P094A.title: Hydraulic Pump Driver Performance
P094A.description: Concerns the electronic driver that powers the motor of a hydraulic or electric oil pump, often a separate pump controller. The driver reports, or the module infers, that it cannot deliver the commanded speed or current although the circuit is not open or shorted. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Hyundai shows what such a driver monitors on its wet 8-speed DCT pumps: overcurrent, current and Hall sensor faults and internal faults, filed under its own P193D and P1C2E codes. Mercedes reports an internal fault of the 722.9 auxiliary oil pump under P0944 instead. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094B and P094C are stuck pump faults, P094D overheating, P094E supply; P0C29 is the equivalent for auxiliary fluid pumps of automatics.

causes.label: Internal fault of the pump controller or driver stage
Pump motor drawing excess current (worn bearings, fluid in motor)
High resistance in supply or ground of the driver

symptoms: Warning light on
Auto stop-start disabled
Delayed engagement or slower shifts

P094B.title: Hydraulic Pump Stuck On
P094B.description: The hydraulic pump keeps running although the module has switched it off, or it never reaches its cut-out point. Causes are a welded relay or shorted driver, or a pump that cannot reach cut-out pressure because of leakage. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. In the pump and accumulator unit of an automated gearbox, described in a ZF patent, the pump should rest once the accumulator is charged. Toyota links a constantly buzzing pump on the MR2 sequential gearbox to fluid loss at the hydraulic power unit, reported under P0942. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094C is the opposite fault, P0946 the relay plausibility fault, P0943 the too-short cycle. Battery drain and pump wear follow.

causes.label: Pump relay contacts welded closed
Leakage or lost accumulator charge keeps pressure below cut-out
Shorted driver stage or supply wire shorted to battery voltage

symptoms: Pump audible after the vehicle is switched off
Discharged battery
Warning light on

P094C.title: Hydraulic Pump Performance/Stuck Off
P094C.description: The pump is commanded on but does not deliver: it does not turn, turns too slowly or produces too little pressure. The module judges this from pressure or speed feedback. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Mercedes reports a comparable condition of the electric auxiliary oil pump on the 722.9 automatic under P0944; its test plan checks connector and fuse, supply voltage, CAN lines and software, then a check valve in the converter housing, before the pump is replaced. Hyundai lists a stuck high-flow pump on its 8-speed DCT as P193E71. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094B is the opposite fault, P094A the driver, P0944 the pressure loss of the whole unit.

causes.label: Air in the pump after service or a suction leak
Seized or failed pump motor
Blocked strainer or leaking check valve
Supply or relay fault stopping the pump

symptoms: Warning light on
Engine restarts at once or stop-start not available
Delayed engagement or lost drive

P094D.title: Hydraulic Pump Over Temperature
P094D.description: The hydraulic or electric oil pump, or its integrated controller, has become too hot. The temperature is usually measured on the controller board and the pump is derated or switched off to protect it. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Hyundai lists the same condition for the high-flow pump of its wet 8-speed DCT as P193D4B, over temperature, and P1C2E92 for the high-pressure pump motor control. Kia recalled stop-start oil pump controllers in 2023 because a damaged capacitor could short and overheat the board, harness and connector. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094A is the driver fault, P094B a pump that never stops, a common reason for heat build-up.

causes.label: Pump running too long because of leakage or a stuck relay
Defective pump controller board
Very hot transmission fluid or blocked cooling

symptoms: Warning light on
Stop-start temporarily disabled
Burning smell near the pump in severe cases

P094E.title: Hydraulic Pump Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P094E.description: Fault in the power feed of the hydraulic or electric oil pump: fuse, supply wire, connector or relay output. The module sees missing or implausible supply at the pump or its controller. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Mercedes shows the checks that belong to it on the electric auxiliary oil pump of the 722.9 automatic, although it reports that pump under P0944: connector and fuse first, then supply voltage and CAN lines. Hyundai lists an open circuit of its DCT high-flow pump as P193D13. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs.
