P0945 to P0948 concern the control side, P094A the driver, P0562 general low system voltage. Without supply the pump stops and stop-start is usually blocked.

causes.label: Blown pump fuse
Open or corroded supply wire or connector
Weak battery or poor main ground lowering pump supply voltage

symptoms: Warning light on
Pump does not run
Stop-start disabled or gearbox in limp mode

P0950.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit
P0950.description: General electrical fault in the circuit that carries the driver's manual up and down requests to the transmission control, as used by tip-shift gates on automatics and by automated manual gearboxes. A Chrysler patent shows the classic design: a transverse gate beside the drive positions with a proximity switch that signals upshift on one side and downshift on the other. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The module typically checks the switch signals for states that cannot occur. P0951 to P0954 are the range, low, high and intermittent faults, P0955 onward the mode select circuit. Usually manual shifting is disabled while normal automatic driving remains available; MIL use varies.

causes.label: Failed up/down switch or sensor in the selector lever or paddles
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the shifter (e.g. after spilled liquid)
Clockspring or steering column wiring fault on paddle-shift vehicles

symptoms: Manual or tip shifting does not respond
Gear display or warning message
Automatic mode still works normally

P0951.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0951.description: Plausibility fault in the circuit that reports the driver's manual upshift and downshift requests, typically the tip gate of an automatic selector lever or steering wheel paddles. The signal is electrically valid but makes no sense, for example both requests active together or a request held far longer than any tap. A Volkswagen patent explains that the Hall elements in such tip gates are hard to diagnose and proposes checking all sensors and lines while the lever sits in P or R. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0950 is the general circuit fault, P0952 to P0954 the low, high and intermittent faults. Usually only manual shifting is disabled.

causes.label: Sticking or worn up/down tip switch, request signal stays active
Displaced magnet or damaged Hall sensor board in the selector lever
Spilled liquid or dirt in the shifter causing cross-talk between contacts
Faulty input stage in the transmission or shifter control module

symptoms: Tip shifting or paddles do not respond or respond erratically
Unwanted gear changes in manual mode
Warning message, automatic mode keeps working

P0952.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Low
P0952.description: The control unit sees the voltage on the manual up/down request circuit below its expected window, typically a signal wire shorted to ground or a switch stuck in the grounded state. In many tip gates the moving contact switches to ground, as a Nissan patent shows, so a short to ground can mimic a permanently held request; a Volkswagen patent describes checking the Hall tip sensors for shorts and breaks while the lever is in P or R. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0953 is the high counterpart, P0950 the general and P0951 the plausibility fault. In practice manual shifting is locked out while D keeps shifting automatically.

causes.label: Signal wire of the up/down circuit chafed through and shorted to ground
Tip switch stuck in the closed position
Moisture or spilled drink in the shifter creating a leakage path to ground
Low supply voltage to a Hall-type tip sensor

symptoms: Manual tip shifting inoperative
Gear indicator shows no manual gear or a warning message
Normal automatic driving in D still possible

P0953.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit High
P0953.description: Voltage on the manual up/down request circuit lies above its expected window. Common reasons are a signal wire shorted to battery voltage or, where the input is pulled up internally, a broken wire or a switch that never closes. A Volkswagen patent names a short to plus and a line break as faults its tip-gate diagnosis detects with the lever in P or R; a Chrysler patent shows the classic AutoStick-style gate with one switch for up and one for down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0952 covers the low side, P0954 dropouts, P0950 the general fault. Manual shifting is usually disabled, automatic mode remains.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to a voltage-carrying wire in the shifter harness
Broken wire or unplugged connector on a pulled-up input
Missing ground of the tip switch or Hall sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Tip gate or paddles have no effect
Warning or message about manual mode
Automatic shifting continues normally

P0954.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Intermittent
P0954.description: The manual up/down request signal drops out or flickers for short moments, so a single tap may arrive twice, late or not at all. Unlike P0952 and P0953 the voltage is not stuck outside its window; it jumps between states without a matching lever movement. Typical triggers are loose pins in the shifter connector, worn contacts or a harness that flexes with the lever. A Chrysler patent shows how simple contact switches in the gate signal each request, a Volkswagen patent how Hall tip sensors and their lines are checked. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks. P0950 is the general fault. The driver notices missed or doubled manual shifts.

causes.label: Loose or spread pins in the selector lever connector
Harness broken internally where it moves with the lever or steering column
Worn or oxidised tip switch contacts

symptoms: Manual shifts occasionally ignored or executed twice
Fault comes and goes, often over bumps
Manual mode temporarily switched off

P0955.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit
P0955.description: Fault in the circuit that tells the transmission control whether the driver has moved the selector lever from D into the manual gate. A Nissan patent shows a dedicated manual mode switch with two contacts on separate inputs, so a break or a short to ground can be told apart; a Hyundai patent uses a microswitch on the lever. Genesis bulletins for 2017-18 G80 and G90 automatics list Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit for the cable-shift version, with a check engine light and a part from the shift lever group as repair, though the table prints the code as P0995 and P095500. So at least Hyundai uses ASM for the manual mode of a torque converter automatic. P0956 to P0959 are the detailed variants, P0950 the up/down request circuit.

causes.label: Failed manual mode switch or microswitch in the selector lever
Corroded or loose connector at the selector lever assembly
Damaged wiring between selector lever and transmission control module

symptoms: Manual mode cannot be selected or is not displayed
Check engine or transmission warning light on
Driving in D remains possible

P0956.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Range/Performance
P0956.description: The manual mode signal is electrically valid but contradicts other information, for example manual mode reported while the range sensor reads P, R or N, or the mode switch never changing although the up/down requests arrive. A Hyundai patent uses a microswitch with two opposing contacts and treats identical or missing signals on both inputs as a defect; a Nissan patent likewise compares two contacts of the manual mode switch. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly, and Hyundai's mode circuit fault is only documented as the general code P0955. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0957 to P0959 cover low, high and intermittent faults. Manual mode is usually blocked.

causes.label: Mode switch or its actuating foot misaligned on the lever
Worn switch contacts giving contradictory states on both inputs
Transmission range sensor out of adjustment, disagrees with the mode signal
Worn selector lever bushings allowing side play

symptoms: Manual mode drops out or will not engage
Display shows manual mode while lever is in D, or the reverse
Warning lamp depending on manufacturer

P0957.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Low
P0957.description: Voltage in the manual mode circuit, the signal that reports the selector lever in the manual gate, is below the expected range. Mostly the signal line has a short to ground or the switch contact hangs in its grounded position. A Nissan patent describes a manual mode switch whose moving contact is grounded and explains how the control unit spots a contact shorted to earth from its two inputs. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; Hyundai's mode circuit fault appears in Genesis bulletins only as the general code. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0958 is the high counterpart, P0955 the general and P0956 the plausibility fault. Expect manual mode to be unavailable or stuck on.

causes.label: Mode signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Mode switch stuck in the grounded position
Liquid or dirt in the selector lever housing

symptoms: Manual mode not available or permanently indicated
Warning lamp depending on manufacturer
Automatic driving in D unaffected

P0958.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit High
P0958.description: The manual mode signal from the selector lever reads above its expected range. Possible causes are a short to supply voltage or, with an internally pulled-up input, an open circuit or missing switch ground that keeps the line high. A Nissan patent explains how two separately wired contacts let the control unit recognise a break in the manual mode switch, and a Hyundai patent shows the lever microswitch that reports the change from D to M. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; Hyundai's mode fault is only documented as P0955. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0957 is the low side, P0959 the intermittent variant. Usually the gearbox stays in automatic mode.

causes.label: Broken mode signal wire or disconnected shifter plug
Missing ground at the mode switch
Mode signal shorted to a voltage-carrying wire

symptoms: Manual gate has no effect, gearbox stays in automatic mode
Warning lamp depending on manufacturer
No manual gear shown on the display

P0959.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Intermittent
P0959.description: The signal reporting the selector lever in the manual gate drops out or toggles briefly while the lever is not moved, so the transmission control switches between manual and automatic mode on its own. The voltage is not stuck out of range as with P0957 or P0958 but jumps. Loose connector pins at the lever, a harness that flexes with the shifter or a worn microswitch are typical. A Hyundai patent shows such a microswitch actuated by the lever's sideways movement, a Nissan patent the two-contact mode switch. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks. P0955 is the general fault, P0954 the intermittent fault of the up/down circuit.

causes.label: Loose pins in the selector lever connector
Worn or bouncing mode microswitch
Harness damaged where it moves with the lever

symptoms: Manual mode switches on or off by itself
Gear display flickers between D and manual gear
Fault often appears on rough roads

P095A.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit C
P095A.description: Circuit C is a third channel reporting the shift position inside an automated manual gearbox, for example a further sensor track or a sensor on another shift rail or selector shaft. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault of that signal that fits none of the more specific C variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, and which sensor carries the letter C depends on the design. A Nissan/Aichi patent describes shift stroke sensors as the feedback for engaging gears, an Aisin AI patent the fallback when a stroke sensor fails. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095B to P095D are the C siblings, P0914 and P091A the same signal on circuits A and B. Shifting may be restricted.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector at shift position sensor C
Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit C
Faulty shift position sensor C
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Slower or restricted gear changes in fallback mode
Gearbox may hold a gear or stay in neutral

P095B.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit C Range/Performance
P095B.description: Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit C of an automated manual gearbox. The voltage is electrically acceptable, but the value does not fit: it contradicts the other position channels, stays put while the shift actuator moves, or misses the learned gear positions. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent points out that sensor mountings on shift parts can give way under vibration and distort the reading; an Aisin AI patent explains how control carries on when a stroke sensor can no longer be trusted. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P095A, P095C and P095D are the electrical faults of circuit C, P0915 and P091B the same check on A and B.

causes.label: Worn or drifting shift position sensor C disagreeing with the other channels
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit

symptoms: Transmission warning light on
Harsh or aborted gear changes
Fallback mode with fewer available gears

P095C.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit C Low
P095C.description: The signal of shift position sensor C in an automated manual gearbox lies below its permitted voltage window. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a sensor with an internal fault pulling its output down. Because the value is physically impossible, the control unit can flag it quickly without comparing it to other channels. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent shows shift stroke sensors as the position feedback for gear engagement, an Aisin AI patent the fallback strategy when such a sensor drops out. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095D is the high counterpart, P095A the general and P095B the plausibility fault; P0916 and P091C are the low faults of A and B.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground
Open or shorted 5 V supply of the sensor
Internally failed shift position sensor C

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Fallback mode with restricted gears
Gearbox may refuse to leave neutral

P095D.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit C High
P095D.description: Shift position sensor C of an automated manual gearbox delivers a voltage above its permitted window. This usually points to a signal wire shorted to the supply, a broken sensor ground or, with a pulled-up input, an interrupted signal line. Since no real shift position produces such a value, the module can set the code without cross-checking other channels. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent describes shift stroke sensors as feedback for gear engagement, an Aisin AI patent how control continues when one of them fails. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095C is the low counterpart, P095A the general and P095B the plausibility fault; P0917 and P091D are the high faults of A and B.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to the 5 V supply or battery voltage
Open ground circuit of the sensor
Internally failed shift position sensor C

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Fallback mode with restricted gears
Jerky or aborted gear changes

P0960.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open
P0960.description: Open-circuit fault in the driver circuit of pressure control solenoid A: the module measures an impedance far above the coil value, as if a wire, pin or winding were broken. Which solenoid carries the letter A depends on the gearbox. Ford uses it for the line pressure (EPC) solenoid; GM's 8-speed for clutch 1 (CB1278R), the 9- and 10-speeds for clutch CB123456(R), Allison 1000 for main modulation (line) pressure and GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the odd-clutch valve. GM flags more than 200 kOhm for 0.3 s (Type A), Allison 173 kOhm or more after an intrusive test. GM six-speeds report an open under P0963 instead. Low and high are P0962/P0963, performance P0961. Expect maximum line pressure, harsh shifts or a fixed limp gear.

causes.label: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body or solenoid assembly
Loose, corroded or pushed-back pin at the transmission connector or pass-through
Broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty output stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission warning or MIL on, fault message in the cluster
Very firm or harsh shifts due to maximum line pressure
Transmission stays in a fixed limp gear

P0961.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0961.description: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid A: the circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid does not behave as commanded. On GM's six-speeds, where A is the line pressure solenoid, the Saab 9-4X 6T70 sets it when measured and commanded current differ for 5 s, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s; both Type B, two trips. Allison 1000 flags a current error of 0.5 A or more in 40 of 80 samples (Type A). Ford's 2023 diesel summary lists it as a PC A current range fault. In GM's CVT, A feeds the secondary pulley: a pressure error above 500 kPa steady or 1,500 kPa transient, confirmed by a ratio error, sets it after 5 s. Electrical faults are P0960, P0962 and P0963. The module usually commands maximum line pressure and freezes adaptations.

causes.label: Solenoid with internal electrical or mechanical fault, current no longer follows the command
Debris or varnish in the fluid sticking the solenoid or regulator valve
High resistance at connector or pass-through distorting the current
Low fluid level causing pressure errors (CVT pulley monitor)

symptoms: Harsh or erratic shifts
MIL or transmission warning after the second drive
Slipping or ratio flare on CVT applications

P0962.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
P0962.description: Pressure control solenoid A circuit low: the driver sees a short to ground. Ford tests its line pressure (EPC) solenoid this way; a short there opens a high-side switch that cuts power to the shift solenoids and leaves park, reverse, neutral and one fixed forward gear at maximum line pressure. On GM's six-speeds and the Saab 9-4X 6T70, A is the line pressure solenoid; the fault matures in 1.5 to 2 s and is Type A, with reverse and 5th gear only, no converter lock-up and maximum line pressure. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use A for a clutch solenoid and treat less than 0.5 ohm as a short, Allison 1000 for main modulation pressure (125 ms). Siblings: P0960 open, P0963 high, P0961 performance.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through and touching ground
Internally shorted solenoid coil
Transmission fluid or water in the connector bridging pins
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL and transmission warning on immediately
Limp mode with only one forward gear and reverse
Harsh engagements, poor acceleration from standstill

P0963.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit High
P0963.description: Pressure control solenoid A circuit high: the driver detects a short to voltage, and on GM's six-speeds also an open circuit, since those units have no separate open code. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (line pressure solenoid) sets it after 5 s as Type B, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s over two trips; the module then commands maximum line pressure and freezes adaptations. Ford tests its line pressure (EPC) solenoid for short to power and, in some applications, keeps P0963 like P0960 without MIL because maximum line pressure does not raise emissions. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds and Allison 1000 (power short within 75 ms) use A for a clutch or main modulation solenoid. Expect firm, harsh shifts rather than slipping. Siblings: P0960, P0961, P0962.

causes.label: Open coil or high-resistance connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or contaminated connector at the transmission
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Firm or harsh shifts at maximum line pressure
Warning light, on some vehicles only after two drives or not at all
Shift adaptation no longer improves

P0964.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open
P0964.description: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid B. What B controls differs by gearbox: GM's 8-speed uses it for clutch 2 (CB12345R), the 9-speed for CB29 and the 10-speed for CB128910R, Allison 1000 for pressure control solenoid 2, and GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the even-clutch pressure valve. GM sets it at more than 200 kOhm for 0.3 s (Type A, one trip), Allison at 173 kOhm or more after an intrusive test, the dual-clutch unit after 150 ms. GM six-speeds do not use P0964; an open in their 3-5-reverse solenoid shows up as P0967. Ford's OBD summaries list no B or C codes. Depending on the clutch involved, gears are lost or the unit drops into a fixed limp gear. Siblings: P0965, P0966, P0967.

causes.label: Open solenoid coil
Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Broken control wire
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL and transmission warning on
Certain gears missing or limp mode
Dual-clutch gearbox drives on one sub-gearbox only

P0965.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0965.description: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid B: wiring is intact, but current or resulting pressure does not match the command. In the Saab 9-4X 6T70, solenoid 2 feeds the 3-5-reverse clutch; a current mismatch for 5 s sets a Type C code without MIL and freezes that clutch's adaptations, and GM's 2016 six-speed table also lists it without MIL. Allison 1000 checks for a current error of 0.5 A or more within 250 ms windows (Type A). In GM's CVT, B controls the primary pulley: a pressure error above 500 kPa steady or 1,500 kPa transient, confirmed by a ratio error for 5 s, sets a Type A code. Electrical faults of B are P0964, P0966 and P0967. Symptoms range from none to rough 3rd, 5th or reverse, or CVT ratio problems.

causes.label: Worn or internally faulty solenoid, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or its regulator valve
Internal leak in the CVT primary pulley circuit
High resistance in connector or pass-through

symptoms: Rough or delayed 3rd, 5th or reverse engagement
CVT ratio fluctuates, engine speed flares
Often no warning light on six-speed applications

P0966.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
P0966.description: Pressure control solenoid B circuit low, meaning a short to ground in the driver circuit. On GM's six-speeds and the Saab 9-4X 6T70, B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch; a short lasting 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) or 1 s (Saab) sets a Type A code with a fixed limp mode: reverse and 5th gear, maximum line pressure, converter clutch off. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use B for a clutch solenoid and treat less than 0.5 ohm as a short; Allison 1000 uses it for pressure control solenoid 2 with ground-short detection in 125 ms. Ford does not use the B codes. Siblings are P0964 open, P0967 high and P0965 performance; solenoids A and C follow the same scheme.

causes.label: Chafed control wire touching ground
Internally shorted solenoid in the valve body assembly
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on immediately
Limp mode with reverse and one forward gear
No torque converter lock-up, higher fuel consumption

P0967.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit High
P0967.description: Pressure control solenoid B circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, since they have no P0964. For the Saab 9-4X 6T70, where B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch, the module needs 1 s, stores a Type A code and limits the transmission to reverse and 3rd gear at maximum line pressure; GM's 2018 six-speed table uses 0.3 s and one trip. GM's 8-speed (clutch 2), the 9- and 10-speeds, Allison 1000 (power short within 75 ms) and GM's dual-clutch gearbox (even-clutch valve) report the same fault on their solenoid B. Ford does not use it. Siblings: P0964 open, P0966 low, P0965 performance. Repairs usually involve the solenoid body or valve body module.

causes.label: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or contaminated transmission connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure
Dual-clutch gearbox loses the even gears

P0968.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open
P0968.description: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid C. GM's 8-speed assigns C to clutch 3 (C13567), the 9-speed to CB38 and the 10-speed to C23457910; an impedance above 200 kOhm for 0.3 s counts as open and sets a Type A code after one trip. In GM's dual-clutch gearbox, C is the redundant shutdown valve of the odd clutch, checked for open load while its output is switched off and confirmed after 150 ms. GM six-speeds report an open C solenoid as P0971, and neither Ford's summaries nor the Allison 1000 tables list C codes. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission output components. Low and high are P0970/P0971, performance P0969; the usual result is a lost gear range or limp mode.

causes.label: Open solenoid coil
Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Broken control wire
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL and transmission warning on
Gears that need clutch C are unavailable
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P0969.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0969.description: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid C. Publicly documented only for GM's front-drive six-speeds: on the Saab 9-4X 6T70, clutch pressure solenoid 3 feeds the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches through the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve. If measured current differs from the commanded current for 5 s, the module stores a Type C code and freezes the adaptations of both clutches. GM's 2016 table (C456/CBR1 solenoid) sets it after an invalid feedback for 4.4 of 5 s, also without MIL. Other GM users such as the 8- to 10-speeds list only open, low and high for C, and Ford does not use C. Drivers rarely notice more than gradually rougher 4-5-6 or reverse engagements. Electrical faults: P0968, P0970, P0971.

causes.label: Solenoid 3 with internal fault, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve
High resistance in the internal connection to the module

symptoms: Usually no warning light
Rougher shifts into 4th, 5th, 6th or reverse over time
Shift adaptation stops learning

P0970.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
P0970.description: Pressure control solenoid C circuit low, a short to ground in the driver. On GM's six-speeds C is the C456/CBR1 solenoid; on the Saab 9-4X 6T70 it is clutch pressure solenoid 3 for the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches. A short for 1 s (Saab) or 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) sets a Type A code: only reverse and 5th gear, no converter lock-up, maximum line pressure. GM's 8-speed uses C for clutch 3 (C13567), the 9- and 10-speeds for CB38 or C23457910 with less than 0.5 ohm counting as a short; GM's dual-clutch gearbox uses it for the odd-clutch shutdown valve. Siblings: P0968 open, P0971 high, P0969 performance. Since the solenoid sits in the valve body, repairs often mean the control solenoid valve assembly.

causes.label: Internally shorted solenoid in the control solenoid valve assembly
Chafed control wire touching ground
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on immediately
Limp mode in reverse and one forward gear
Weak acceleration from standstill

P0971.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit High
P0971.description: Pressure control solenoid C circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, as there is no separate open code there. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (clutch pressure solenoid 3, low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches) and GM's 2018 six-speed table set it after 1 s or 0.3 s as Type A, with limp mode in reverse and 5th gear at maximum line pressure. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use the code for their clutch solenoid C; GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the redundant odd-clutch shutdown valve, where too high a voltage at the sense pin with the output switched on counts as a short. Ford does not use C codes. Siblings: P0968 open, P0970 low, P0969 performance. A loose connector can make the fault come and go.

causes.label: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or loose transmission connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure
Fault comes and goes with temperature or vibration

P0972.title: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0972.description: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A: the circuit is not plainly shorted, yet its electrical behaviour does not fit what the module commands. Today's large makers rarely use the code. GM's 2007 table for the Allison 1000 six-speed used it for an open SS1 circuit: after three hardware fault samples the module opens the low-side driver as an intrusive test and reports P0972 if four more samples show no short to ground (400 ms, Type A, MIL at once). Newer GM Allison tables move that open to P097A. Ferrari's DCT bulletin reuses P0972 for a missing signal from the actuator 1 engage position sensor, not a solenoid. Ford and GM six-speeds report opens elsewhere. Shorts are P0973/P0974.

causes.label: Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid A (Allison-type usage)
Loose or corroded terminal at the transmission connector or internal harness
Chafed or broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: MIL or transmission warning on
Transmission falls back to a fixed default gear
Missing or abrupt shifts

P0973.title: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
P0973.description: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A, usually a short to ground. Ford lists it as SSA short to ground beside P0750 (open) for the 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140, checked by a driver feedback line within 0.5 to 5 s. GM six-speeds (6L/6T) call SS A the mode 2 solenoid and set P0973 after 1.2 of 1.5 s, MIL after one trip. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 needs 2 s, Type A, then only reverse and 5th remain. GM's 2016 Allison 1000 table folds ground short (0.42 ohm or less) and open (200 kOhm or more) into this code over 10 counts. Saab's Aisin gearbox in the 9-5 (2010) maps it to shift solenoid valve 2. High side is P0974.

causes.label: Control wire to solenoid A chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid A or the control solenoid assembly
Fluid or metal debris bridging pins at the transmission connector
Faulty low-side driver in the transmission or powertrain module

symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip on many vehicles
Limp mode with only a few gears, often reverse plus one forward gear
Harsh engagements due to maximum line pressure
Torque converter lockup and manual shifting disabled

P0974.title: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit High
P0974.description: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A. What it covers depends on the maker. Ford reserves it for a short to power on SSA, because an open SSA circuit sets P0750. GM six-speeds put both an open and a power short of the mode 2 solenoid here: 1.2 of 1.5 s, MIL only after two trips. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 waits 2 s, Type B, and then blocks 1st gear. GM's Allison 1000 tables of 2016 and 2023 treat it as a pure power short (0.39 ohm or less, 3 samples, 75 or 60 ms) and report opens separately. Saab's Aisin gearbox in the 9-5 (2010) sets it when solenoid valve 2 reads off while commanded on, 100 ms five times, Type A. Ground-side faults are P0973.

causes.label: Open coil or broken wire where the maker reports opens under the high code (GM six-speed)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Spread or corroded pins at the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on, on GM six-speeds only after a second faulty trip
First gear locked out, start-off in a higher gear
Missing or wrong shifts, possibly limp mode

P0975.title: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0975.description: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Three documented uses differ widely. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS2 circuit, confirmed by an intrusive low-side test (400 ms, Type A). FCA's 2016 recall for the 9-speed front-drive transaxle (Cherokee, 200, Renegade, 500X, ProMaster City) names P0975 with P0978, P0981 and P0984 as the codes set by intermittent high resistance from poorly crimped terminals in the range sensor harness under old TCM software; updated software reports that case as P0901 instead. Ferrari's DCT uses P0975 for a missing actuator 2 position signal. Low/high are P0976/P0977.

causes.label: Poorly crimped terminals causing intermittent high resistance (FCA 9-speed recall)
Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid B
Outdated transmission software that misreads harness resistance
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: MIL or transmission warning on
Unexpected shift to neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed)
Fixed default gear or harsh shifts

P0976.title: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
P0976.description: Low-voltage fault, normally a ground short, in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. On GM six-speeds SS B is the mode 3 multiplex valve; the 2016 table sets P0976 after 1.2 of 1.5 s without lighting the MIL, while the Saab 9-4X 6T70 version needs 2 s, is Type B and raises line pressure. Ford uses it for SSB short to ground, with P0755 for an open; on the 2023 Super Duty diesel SSB is fed by solenoid supply TSPC2, so a P2669 supply fault disables this check. GM's Allison 1000 merges ground short and open into it in 2016, but from 2022 reports opens as P097B and keeps P0976 for ground faults found by an intrusive test (120 ms, MIL after one trip). High side is P0977.

causes.label: Solenoid B control wire shorted to ground or housing
Internal short in solenoid B or its valve body assembly
Moisture or debris bridging pins at the connector
Faulty driver in the transmission control module

symptoms: Warning light or stored code, on some GM six-speeds without MIL
Firm shifts due to raised line pressure
Gears missing or limp mode

P0977.title: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit High
P0977.description: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. GM six-speeds put an open or a power short of the mode 3 multiplex valve here, 1.2 of 1.5 s; the 2016 table sets it without MIL, the 2019 table with MIL after one trip. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 treats it more severely than P0976: 2 s, Type A, high-side driver off, only reverse and 5th gear left, no converter lockup. Ford uses it strictly for SSB short to power, as in its 2012 and later summaries. GM's Allison 1000 checks for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three samples (75 ms in 2016, 60 ms in 2023). FCA 9-speed and Aisin uses are not documented for this code. Ground-side faults are P0976.

causes.label: Open solenoid B coil or wire on GM six-speeds, where opens report as high
Control wire shorted to battery or a switched supply
Damaged pins or seals at the transmission pass-through connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Limp mode with only reverse and one high forward gear
Weak acceleration from rest
MIL or transmission warning, depending on calibration

P0978.title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0978.description: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS3 circuit, but only while the commanded gear is not reverse trim, 5th or 6th; the table even prints the label Circuit Low beside an open-circuit test, an apparent typo. FCA lists P0978 among the four codes that the 2014–2016 9-speed transaxle set under old software when the range sensor harness had poor crimps. Ferrari's DCT bulletin uses it for a missing signal from the actuator 4 engage position sensor. Ford and GM six-speeds do not use it. Low/high are P0979/P0980, the current open code P097C.

causes.label: Intermittent high resistance at crimped harness terminals (FCA 9-speed)
Open coil of shift solenoid C (Allison-type usage)
Transmission software that predates the manufacturer's fix
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: MIL or transmission warning on
Sudden neutral or default gear while driving
Erratic or missing shifts

P0979.title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
P0979.description: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid C. GM uses it mainly on the Allison 1000 six-speed of its heavy pickups and chassis cabs: in 2016 a ground short of 0.22 ohm or less, stricter than the 0.42 ohm for SS1 and SS2, or an open of 200 kOhm or more counts after 10 samples (250 ms, Type A). From 2022 the open moves to P097C and P0979 needs an intrusive low-side test (120 ms, MIL after one trip). The Allison PS3 pressure switch test (P0872) also points to P0979 when its fault is electrical. Ford uses it for SSC short to ground beside P0760 open; on 6R80 and 6F, SSC drives the CB26 clutch. High side is P0980.

causes.label: Solenoid C control wire shorted to ground
Internal short of solenoid C inside the valve body
Open coil on GM 2016 Allison calibrations, which report opens under this code
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip
Transmission holds a default gear
Rough or delayed shifts involving the affected clutch

P097A.title: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open
P097A.description: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A, a code that later J2012 editions added; older lists still show P097A as reserved. GM is the only maker found that documents it: the 2022 to 2025 tables for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its heavy-duty trucks call it Shift Solenoid 1 Control Circuit Open. After one hardware fault the module flags pending, and after three samples it opens the low-side driver as a test; three more open readings at 9 to 18 V set the code (120 ms, MIL after one trip). The same gearbox once used P0972 for this and P0973 in 2016. Ford reports an open SSA as P0750, GM six-speeds as P0974, and Genesis folds all electrical faults of A into P0753.

causes.label: Open coil of shift solenoid 1/A
Unplugged, corroded or pushed-out pin at the transmission connector
Broken wire in the internal or external transmission harness
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip
Transmission in a fixed default gear
Shifts involving solenoid A missing

P097B.title: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open
P097B.description: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Public use is again limited to GM's Allison 1000 six-speed in heavy-duty trucks, where the 2022 to 2025 tables label it Shift Solenoid 2 Control Circuit Open. SS2 shares high-side driver 2 with SS1 and SS3, so the open test only runs while that supply is on and free of P2669, P2670 or P2671. It confirms an open by switching the low-side driver off and needs three samples, 120 ms, MIL after one trip. Allison's 2007 table filed the same check as P0975, the 2016 table under P0976. Ford reports an open SSB as P0755, GM six-speeds as P0977. Low/high are P0976/P0977.

causes.label: Open coil of shift solenoid 2/B
Loose or corroded terminal on the solenoid B circuit
Wire broken by vibration or heat near the transmission
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip
Default gear operation, some ranges unavailable
Harsh or missing shifts

P097C.title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open
P097C.description: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its 2022 to 2025 heavy-duty tables as Shift Solenoid 3 Control Circuit Open, with the same intrusive low-side test as SS1 and SS2: three samples, 120 ms, battery 9 to 18 V, MIL after one trip. It is the youngest of three codes for this one fault on that gearbox: 2007 used P0978, only outside reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear, 2016 merged it into P0979 with a 200 kOhm limit. Ford reports an open SSC under P0760, and no other maker was found using P097C. A related pressure switch code may set too, because SS3 strokes the S3 valve that switch PS3 watches.

causes.label: Open coil of shift solenoid 3/C
Loose, wet or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid C
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip
Upper gears unavailable or fixed default gear
Possible additional pressure switch code

P097D.title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit/Open
P097D.description: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. No maker documents this code publicly. GM's Allison tables that use P097A to P097C stop at shift solenoid 3, and Ford, which has a solenoid D in its 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140 gearboxes, reports an open SSD under the base code P0765, with P0982/P0983 for ground and power shorts. Any use would follow the CARB rule that every transmission output must be checked for lack of circuit continuity, plus the pattern of the A to C codes: a high-impedance reading confirmed by switching the driver. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F, SSD feeds either CBLR or C456 through a multiplex valve, so an open there would disturb first and upper gears alike.

causes.label: Open coil of shift solenoid D
Disconnected or corroded terminal in the solenoid D circuit
Broken wire in the transmission harness
Faulty driver in the control module

symptoms: Warning light or MIL on
Missing gears that depend on solenoid D
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P097E.title: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit/Open
P097E.description: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. No manufacturer was found that documents this code. Ford, the main user of an SSE, still reports an open SSE under P0770; its 2023 diesel summary pairs that with P0985 for ground and P0986 for power shorts, and powers SSE from supply TSPC1 together with SSA and SSC. In the 6R80 and 6F, SSE is an on/off solenoid that switches the multiplexing of SSD, while the 6R140 uses a variable force SSE for clutch C456. Without a public owner the code rests on the CARB demand for circuit continuity checks on transmission outputs and on GM's A to C pattern. Opens in shared supply wiring usually set P0657 first.

causes.label: Open coil of shift solenoid E
Poor contact at the solenoid E terminal or lead frame
Broken signal wire to solenoid E
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Warning light or MIL on
Gears using solenoid E unavailable
Default gear operation

P097F.title: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit/Open
P097F.description: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid F. It is the only code in its family for letter F, since J2012 has no range/performance, low or high codes for F in this block. No maker was found to document it. Hyundai's Genesis bulletin for the eight-speed (2017–2018 G80 and G90) shows how F is handled in practice: an electrical fault of shift control solenoid F (labelled 8LR) is reported under P2709 and fixed by replacing the solenoid. Other makers with six or more clutches use their own codes. A P097F would follow the CARB requirement to test every transmission output for circuit continuity, by analogy with GM's open tests for solenoids 1 to 3.

causes.label: Open coil of shift solenoid F
Loose or corroded terminal at the valve body connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid F
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Warning light or MIL on
Gears that need solenoid F unavailable
Limp mode

P0980.title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit High
P0980.description: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid C, meaning a short to supply. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed: the 2007 table wants four consecutive power-short samples (100 ms, Type A) and skips the check in reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear; later tables (2016, 2018) look for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three counts within 75 ms, and from 2022 within 60 ms, MIL after one trip. Ford uses it for SSC short to power in all its listed gearboxes, with P0760 for an open. Neither GM's 6L/6T six-speeds nor Saab's documented gearboxes use P0980. The ground counterpart is P0979, the open code for the Allison is P097C.

causes.label: Solenoid C control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Shorted turns in solenoid C lowering its resistance
Adjacent pins bridged by fluid or debris in the connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip
Solenoid C stuck energized, wrong gear or default gear
Harsh shifts

P0981.title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0981.description: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. GM's Allison tables end at solenoid C, and Ford checks SSD only with P0765, P0982 and P0983, so the large North American users skip it. Two codegenau sources exist. FCA's recall S55 (NHTSA 16V-529) covers about 323,400 vehicles with the 9-speed front-drive transaxle; with old TCM software, intermittent high resistance from weak crimps in the range sensor harness could set P0981 or its siblings, and the remedy is new software plus, if a code is present, a new harness. Ferrari's DCT bulletin uses P0981 for a missing signal from the actuator 3 position sensor. Low/high for D are P0982/P0983.

causes.label: Weak terminal crimps causing intermittent resistance (FCA recall S55)
Transmission software not yet updated by the recall
Solenoid D coil resistance out of range
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Unexpected shift to neutral while driving (FCA 9-speed)
MIL or transmission warning on
Default gear or harsh shifts

P0982.title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Low
P0982.description: Low-voltage fault, in practice a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford is the documented user: its summaries list SSD with P0765 open, P0982 short to ground and P0983 short to power, checked continuously through the driver feedback within 0.5 to 5 s. Which clutch this hits depends on the gearbox. In the 6R80 and 6F, SSD is a variable force solenoid feeding CBLR or C456 via the SSE multiplex valve; in the 6R140 it drives CBLR alone. In the 2023 diesel summary SSD is fed from supply TSPC2 with SSB, the converter clutch and line pressure solenoid. GM's six-speed and Allison tables do not use P0982. Ferrari reuses it for an actuator 3 sensor reading too low.

causes.label: Solenoid D control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid D or the main control assembly
Damaged internal lead frame or connector inside the transmission
Faulty driver in the powertrain or transmission module

symptoms: MIL on and default gear operation
No engine braking in first or no reverse, depending on gearbox
Harsh shifts into upper gears

P0983.title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit High
P0983.description: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford defines it narrowly as SSD short to power; the open circuit stays with P0765. On the 6R140 the solenoid outputs are run by a smart driver chip (ADLER) that does the open and short checks itself, while older units use a feedback line from the output stage; both need 0.5 to 5 s. Since SSD on Ford six-speeds controls the low/reverse clutch, either alone or through the multiplex valve, a constant power short can apply that clutch at the wrong time. The 2020–2023 gasoline summary keeps the same assignment. GM documents no P0983 for its geared automatics, and Ferrari uses it for an actuator 3 sensor reading too high. Ground faults are P0982.

causes.label: Solenoid D control wire shorted to a supply
Solenoid D with shorted windings
Conductive contamination between neighbouring pins
Faulty smart driver or output stage in the module

symptoms: MIL on, default gear
Clunk or tie-up feel if the low/reverse clutch applies unintentionally
Upper gears blocked

P0984.title: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0984.description: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford checks SSE with P0770, P0985 and P0986 only, GM's documented tables never reach letter E, and even Ferrari's DCT list, which reuses most of its neighbours, skips P0984. The one codegenau source is FCA: in recall S55 for the 9-speed front-drive transaxle it names P0984 together with P0975, P0978 and P0981. Under old TCM software, a range sensor harness with poor crimps and intermittent high resistance could set them; with new software the same fault shows as P0901, and these four codes then point to a separate transmission problem. Otherwise the code rests only on the CARB rule for transmission output checks. Low/high are P0985/P0986.

causes.label: Range sensor harness with weak crimps (FCA 9-speed recall)
TCM software below the recall level
Internal transmission fault when the code returns after the update
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Sudden neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed)
MIL or transmission warning on
Limp mode

P0985.title: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Low
P0985.description: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford lists it for SSE on the 5R110W and 6R140 and in its 2020–2023 gasoline and 2023 diesel summaries, beside P0770 for an open; for the 6R80 and 6F, whose SSE is the on/off multiplex solenoid, the 2012 text names only P0770. Saab's 2010 9-5 with the Aisin six-speed uses P0985 differently, for shift solenoid valve 1: the module sees the circuit reading on while it is commanded off, 100 ms five times in a row, Type A; it then turns all solenoids off and freezes adaptation. Voltage must be 10.2 to 15.5 V and the engine above 400 rpm. High side is P0986.

causes.label: Solenoid E control wire shorted to ground
Internal short of solenoid E
Water or fluid in the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the transmission module

symptoms: MIL on after the fault is confirmed
All solenoids off, fixed fail-safe gear (Saab/Aisin)
Missing upper gears on Ford gearboxes

P0986.title: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit High
P0986.description: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford means a short to power on SSE; an open sets P0770 and a ground short P0985. On the 6R140 SSE is a variable force solenoid for the C456 clutch, so a short to power can hold that clutch on. Saab's 2010 9-5 with the Aisin six-speed instead assigns P0986 to shift solenoid valve 1 and sets it when the circuit reads off although it is commanded on, which also catches an open coil: 100 ms, five times, Type A, all solenoids then switched off. GM's published transmission tables do not use the code. Because makers split opens differently, check the maker's table before replacing parts.

causes.label: Solenoid E control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open coil or wire where the maker reads it as high (Saab/Aisin)
Bent or corroded terminals at the solenoid E connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on, transmission in fail-safe gear
Tie-up or harsh shift if the controlled clutch stays applied
Adaptation frozen, shift quality worsens

P0987.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit
P0987.description: General circuit fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The only public user of switch E found, GM's 6T70/6T75 family (Saab 9-4X: switch 5 on the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutch regulator valve), reports only P0989 and P0990 for it, both as plausibility counts. P0987 is the slot for a module that sees a generic circuit fault on a fifth pressure sensor or switch, for example an open or out-of-range signal, without separating low from high. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs. Range/performance is P0988, low and high are P0989/P0990; switches A to D use P0840 to P0878. Typical effects are frozen shift adaptations and harsher shifts.

causes.label: Failed pressure sensor or switch E
Open or shorted signal wire or poor connector contact
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Warning light depending on manufacturer
Harsher or less consistent shifts
Possible limp mode

P0988.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Range/Performance
P0988.description: Range/performance fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the commanded clutch state or the pressure expected from other inputs. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's 6T70/6T75 family, the one public user of switch E (switch 5 on the low/reverse and 4-5-6 regulator valve), folds such plausibility checks into P0989 and P0990; its switch logic table shows which gears should pressurise the switch. Sonnax describes how these normally closed film switches in the valve body module fail through debris or delaminated films. CARB requires rationality checks of transmission inputs. Siblings: P0987 circuit, P0989 low, P0990 high.

causes.label: Damaged or delaminated switch film, switch reacts late or not at all
Debris in the fluid holding the switch or its regulator valve
Low fluid level or real pressure deviation in the clutch circuit

symptoms: Often no noticeable symptom at first
Shift quality worsens because adaptation stops
Warning light depending on manufacturer

P0989.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
P0989.description: Pressure switch E reads low, meaning no pressure, when it should show pressure. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; the normally closed switch sees pressure while both the low/reverse and the 4-5-6 clutch are released. The module counts clutch releases after which the signal stays low, checked with commanded clutch pressure at 50 kPa or less: 18 counts in GM's 2011 tables and on the Saab 9-4X, 17 in the 2016 table. It is a Type C or Special No Trip code without MIL, and the adaptations of both clutches are frozen. Sonnax lists P0989 among typical switch failures in this valve body module. P0990 is the stuck-high counterpart; switches A to D use P0840 to P0878.

causes.label: Damaged or delaminated film in switch 5 of the valve body module
Debris keeping pressure away from the switch
R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve sticking
Low fluid level

symptoms: No warning light, code stored only
Shifts into 4th to 6th or reverse gradually less smooth
Occasional limp mode if the fault persists

P0990.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit High
P0990.description: Pressure switch E reads high, meaning pressure, when it should be vented. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; applying the low/reverse or 4-5-6 clutch moves that valve and should exhaust the switch. If the signal stays high after such an apply, with commanded clutch pressure at 700 kPa or more, the module counts it: 15 counts on the Saab 9-4X, 30 in GM's 2016 table. It is a Type C or Special No Trip code, so no MIL, and the adaptations of both clutches are frozen. According to Saab, normal debris in the fluid can set it intermittently without noticeable symptoms. A short to voltage on the signal wire has the same effect. P0989 is the stuck-low case.

causes.label: Switch 5 stuck open by a damaged film or debris
R1/4-5-6 regulator valve not moving, switch stays pressurised
Signal circuit shorted to voltage or open inside the module

symptoms: No warning light, code stored only
Intermittent occurrence without noticeable symptoms
Shift quality declines over time

P0991.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent
P0991.description: The module has seen the signal of the fifth transmission pressure sensor or switch drop out or jump briefly, without a steady low or high reading. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The only switch E found in public sources is GM's TFP switch 5 in the 6T70/6T75 valve body module (Saab 9-4X 2011), a normally closed switch that GM monitors only through P0989 and P0990: signal stuck low at commanded pressure of 50 kPa or less, or stuck high, counted over clutch releases and logged as Special No Trip without MIL. An intermittent check would follow the CARB rule that transmission inputs be monitored for circuit faults. Steady faults are P0987 to P0990. Expect frozen shift adaptation and the odd harsh shift.

causes.label: Loose or corroded contact at the valve body module connector
Debris or damaged diaphragm film making the switch contact flicker
Chafed internal harness that shorts or opens under vibration
Fault in the transmission control module input stage

symptoms: Stored fault, often without warning light
Occasional harsh or flared shift
Shift adaptation frozen

P0992.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit
P0992.description: General circuit fault of a sixth transmission pressure sensor or switch, labelled F. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no gearbox with a switch F was found. GM's six-speeds stop at TFP switch 5 (letter E, P0989/P0990), and Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed monitors its 2-6 brake, high clutch and low-reverse brake switches under P0846, P0876 and P0988, which are letters B, D and E. Pressure switches like these sit in the valve body module and tell the module which clutch is applied; Sonnax describes them as normally closed film-and-piston switches. P0992 would be the code for an open or implausible circuit without a low/high split, as CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs. Range/performance, low, high and intermittent are P0993 to P0996.

causes.label: Open or damaged signal wire or connector to the switch
Pressure switch or sensor failed inside the valve body module
Transmission control module input fault

symptoms: Warning light depending on manufacturer calibration
Harsh or delayed shifts
Possible limp mode with a fixed gear

P0993.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Range/Performance
P0993.description: Pressure sensor or switch F is electrically intact, but its reading does not match what the module expects from the commanded clutch state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest documented logic is GM's for switch E (TFP switch 5, 6T70/6T75): the module checks after each clutch release whether the switch returns to its exhausted state and counts failures, at 50 kPa or less commanded pressure for the low case. A sixth switch would be checked the same way, plausibility against commanded pressure and gear, which CARB requires for transmission inputs. Typical causes are sticking regulator valves, debris and worn switch films rather than wiring. P0992 is the plain circuit fault, P0994/P0995 are low and high.

causes.label: Sticking clutch regulator valve feeding the switch
Worn or delaminated switch film, debris in the switch
Low or contaminated transmission fluid

symptoms: Harsh or flared shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Warning light depending on calibration

P0994.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Low
P0994.description: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. With a normally closed switch as described by Sonnax for GM's valve body modules, low means the contacts stay closed, so the module sees no pressure where pressure should be, or the signal wire is shorted to ground. GM's equivalent for switch E, P0989, flags a low signal when commanded pressure is 50 kPa or less and handles it as Special No Trip without MIL; Saab's 9-4X text gives 0 V as the low state and 12 V as high. For an analogue sensor, low would mean a voltage below its valid range. CARB requires such out-of-range checks on transmission inputs. P0995 is the high counterpart.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Switch stuck closed by debris or damaged film
Clutch circuit not reaching pressure (valve or seal leak)

symptoms: Harsh or delayed shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Possible limp mode

P0995.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit High
P0995.description: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays high: with a normally closed switch the contacts stay open, which looks like permanent pressure, or the wire is open or shorted to voltage. No manufacturer documents this use publicly. Hyundai/Genesis bulletins 17-AT-001-G and 21-AT-016HG list P0995 in their subject lines, but their tables pair it with Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit (SBC), and 21-AT-016HG prints the DTC as P095500; this is a misprint for P0955 and does not count as a use of P0995. GM's matching switch E code P0990 is a Special No Trip without MIL; Saab's 9-4X text treats an open and a short to voltage alike as high. CARB requires such checks on transmission inputs. P0994 is the low side.

causes.label: Open signal wire or unplugged connector
Signal wire shorted to voltage
Switch stuck open inside the valve body module

symptoms: Harsh or delayed shifts
Shift adaptation frozen
Possible limp mode

P0996.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Intermittent
P0996.description: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F drops out or flickers for short moments without staying low or high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no transmission with a sixth pressure switch was found: GM's six-speeds end at switch 5 (E), Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed uses letters B, D and E. Because such switches are thin film-and-piston units inside the valve body module, as Sonnax shows, debris or a delaminated film can make the contact chatter, and connector or harness faults do the same electrically. CARB requires transmission inputs to be checked for circuit faults; an intermittent code is the slot for faults too short to set P0994 or P0995. Expect occasional rough shifts, often without a warning light.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector contact
Debris or delaminated film making the switch chatter
Chafed harness shorting or opening under vibration

symptoms: Stored fault, often without warning light
Occasional rough or flared shift

P0997.title: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0997.description: The drive circuit of shift solenoid F works electrically but its measured current or voltage does not fit the command. No manufacturer was found to document this code. The users of the F block, Nissan's RE0F11A CVT and a 2019 Mitsubishi six-speed, list only P0998 and P0999. FCA's nine-speed bulletin 21-019-17 (2015 Chrysler 200 and Jeep Cherokee) shows how the slot is used for solenoids 2 to 5, with P0975, P0978, P0981 and P0984 for control circuit performance, but stops before a sixth solenoid. Genesis reports an electrical fault of its solenoid F under P2709 instead. CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for proper function. P097F is the open circuit, P0998/P0999 low and high.

causes.label: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High-resistance connector or harness contact
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Warning light depending on calibration
Missing or harsh shifts into gears using this solenoid
Possible limp mode

P0998.title: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit Low
P0998.description: Low-voltage fault, typically a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid F. Two makers document it. Nissan lists P0998 as shift solenoid F in bulletin NTB15-037 for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT, whose two-speed auxiliary gearbox uses a low brake, a high clutch and a reverse brake; if the shop manual check points to the transaxle, the bulletin has only the control valve replaced. Mitsubishi's 2019 service manual for a six-speed automatic names P0998/P0999 the low clutch shift solenoid valve system and counts it among faults that can cause gear ratio errors. CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for circuit faults. P0999 is high, P097F open.

causes.label: Solenoid or valve body (control valve) internal fault
Control wire shorted to ground in harness or connector
Transmission control module driver fault

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode or loss of a gear range
Harsh engagement or flare when shifting

P0999.title: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit High
P0999.description: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid F, from a short to voltage or, where the driver uses a pull-up, an open coil or wire. Nissan's bulletin NTB15-037 for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT names P0999 together with P0998 as shift solenoid F and calls for replacing the control valve rather than the whole CVT when diagnosis confirms the fault. Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed assigns P0998/P0999 to the low clutch shift solenoid; for its sister valve G it detects an open circuit as a high reading. Other makers handle F elsewhere: Genesis under P2709, Ford's summaries stop at solenoid E. CARB requires output circuit checks. P0998 is the low side.

causes.label: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body
Open control wire or short to voltage
Connector pin pushed out or corroded

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode or loss of a gear range
Harsh shifts

P099A.title: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit Range/Performance
P099A.description: The drive circuit of shift solenoid G is electrically intact, but current or voltage feedback does not fit the command. No manufacturer was found to document this code. The two documented users of the G control circuit codes report only the hard faults: Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed (low-reverse brake shift solenoid) uses P099B for a short and P099C for an open, and Nissan's RE0F11A CVT lists P099B/P099C. Hyundai and Genesis report their on/off solenoid G under P075A and P075D. The slot would follow the pattern FCA uses for solenoids 2 to 5 (P0975 to P0984, control circuit performance). CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for function. Low and high are P099B/P099C, open P09A0.

causes.label: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High-resistance connector or harness contact
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Warning light depending on calibration
Harsh or missing shifts involving this solenoid
Possible limp mode

P099B.title: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit Low
P099B.description: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid G. Mitsubishi's 2019 service manual for a six-speed automatic uses it for the low-reverse brake shift solenoid: with transmission relay voltage at 2 V or more and the solenoid commanded on, the module sets P099B if the actual voltage stays below 3.7 V for 0.5 s. The check runs continuously; the solenoid is normally energised only in reverse and first-gear coasting. Nissan lists P099B as shift solenoid G in bulletin NTB15-037 for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT and replaces the control valve when diagnosis confirms it. P099C is the high side, P09A0 the generic open.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground in harness or connector
Shorted solenoid inside the valve body
Transmission control module driver fault

symptoms: Check engine light
No reverse or no engine braking in first gear (Mitsubishi)
Limp mode

P099C.title: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit High
P099C.description: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid G. Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed uses P099C for an open circuit of the low-reverse brake shift solenoid: with the solenoid commanded off and transmission relay voltage of 2 V or more, a reading of 3.7 V or more for 0.5 s sets the code. So on this design an open shows up as high, not under P09A0. The drive cycle needs only 10 s with the ignition on. Causes named are the harness, connectors, the TCM and the solenoid in the valve body. Nissan lists P099C as shift solenoid G for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT, with control valve replacement as the fix. P099B is the low side, P099A performance.

causes.label: Open control wire or connector between module and valve body
Open solenoid coil inside the valve body
Control wire shorted to voltage

symptoms: Check engine light
No reverse or harsh reverse engagement (Mitsubishi)
Limp mode

P099D.title: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit Range/Performance
P099D.description: Electrical feedback from the drive circuit of shift solenoid H does not fit the command, although no hard short or open is seen. No manufacturer was found to document this code. Solenoid H means an eighth shift solenoid. The only documented H user, the 2017–2018 Genesis G80 and G90, reports its on/off solenoid for the shift-by-wire park function under P076A and P076D, outside this block. Ford's OBD summaries describe shift solenoid checks only up to E, with separate open, short to ground and short to power codes and 0.5 to 5 s electrical monitoring. CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for proper function. Low and high are P099E/P099F, the open circuit is P09A1.

causes.label: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High-resistance connector or harness contact
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Warning light depending on calibration
Harsh or missing shifts involving this solenoid

P099E.title: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit Low
P099E.description: Low-voltage fault, typically a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid H. No manufacturer was found to document this code. A solenoid H exists only on transmissions with eight or more shift solenoids; Genesis' 2017–2018 G80/G90, the one documented H user, reports its park-function on/off solenoid under P076A and P076D. The closest documented logic is from lower letters: Mitsubishi detects a short on its solenoid G when the voltage stays below 3.7 V for 0.5 s while commanded on, and Ford's summaries store separate short-to-ground codes for solenoids A to E, checked continuously. CARB requires such circuit checks on transmission outputs. P099F is the high side, P09A1 the open circuit.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Shorted solenoid coil
Transmission control module driver fault

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P099F.title: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit High
P099F.description: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid H, from a short to voltage or, on pull-up driver designs, an open coil or wire. No manufacturer was found to document this code. Genesis' 2017–2018 G80/G90 shift-by-wire, the only documented H user, files its park-function on/off solenoid under P076A and P076D, and bulletin 21-AT-016HG fixes it by replacing valve and electronic module. For the high-side logic, Mitsubishi's six-speed is the nearest model: on solenoid G it treats 3.7 V or more for 0.5 s while commanded off as an open circuit. Ford's summaries give short to power its own code for each of solenoids A to E. CARB requires output circuit checks. P099E is the low side.

causes.label: Open control wire or connector
Control wire shorted to voltage
Open solenoid coil

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P09A0.title: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit/Open
P09A0.description: Open circuit or general circuit fault in the drive of shift solenoid G. It is a late addition to J2012: older code lists still show P09A0 to P09FF as reserved. No manufacturer was found to document it. The known users of the G block send opens elsewhere: Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed reports an open low-reverse brake shift solenoid as P099C, Nissan's RE0F11A CVT lists only P099B/P099C, and Hyundai/Genesis use P075A and P075D for their on/off solenoid G. Ford shows the usual split for solenoids A to E, with the open in the base code (P0750 and so on) and separate ground and power shorts. CARB requires every transmission output to be checked for circuit continuity. P099A to P099C are performance, low and high.

causes.label: Broken control wire or unplugged connector
Open solenoid coil
Pin backed out of the connector housing

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P09A1.title: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit/Open
P09A1.description: Open circuit or general circuit fault in the drive of shift solenoid H, the eighth shift solenoid. Like P09A0 it is a late J2012 addition that older code lists still show as reserved. No manufacturer was found to document it. Genesis' 2017–2018 G80/G90, the only documented H user, reports its park-function on/off solenoid under P076A and P076D, and bulletin 21-AT-016HG has valve and electronic module replaced for those. Ford's summaries show what an open check looks like for solenoids A to E: a separate open code, run continuously with 0.5 to 5 s of electrical monitoring. CARB requires every transmission output to be checked for circuit continuity. P099D to P099F cover performance, low and high of solenoid H.

causes.label: Broken control wire or unplugged connector
Open solenoid coil
Pin backed out of the connector housing

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode or missing gears

P09A2.title: Gate Select Position Circuit B
P09A2.description: General electrical fault on the second gate select position signal (circuit B) of an automated manual gearbox. The published designs from Isuzu (one select potentiometer) and Aisin AI (one select stroke sensor) show only a single sensor, so it is not documented whether B is a redundant second track of that sensor or a separate sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P09A4 and P09A5 are the more specific low and high faults of circuit B, P09A3 its plausibility fault; unlike circuit A (P0908) there is no intermittent variant. P0904 and P09A6 cover circuits A and C. Expect shifting to be restricted.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or wet connector at the select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken signal wire of circuit B near the gearbox
Faulty select sensor, often integrated in the shift and select actuator
Faulty input stage for circuit B in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox shifts slowly or locks out certain gears
Gearbox stays in one gear or neutral

P09A3.title: Gate Select Position Circuit B Range/Performance
P09A3.description: Plausibility fault of gate select circuit B: the signal is electrically valid but does not match what the module expects. That could be the reading of circuit A, the learned gate positions, or the target gate the module has commanded, as in the Aisin AI select control that compares actual and target gate. Which comparison applies depends on whether B is a redundant track or a separate sensor, and no manufacturer publishes that or uses this code in citable material. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P09A2, P09A4 and P09A5 are electrical faults of B, P0905 and P09A7 the same check on circuits A and C. A fallback mode with limited shifting is likely.

causes.label: Worn or drifting select sensor, signal B no longer agrees with the reference
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or module replacement
Contact resistance at connector pins distorting signal B
Sluggish or worn select mechanism so the measured gate lags the commanded one

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gate selected or gears refused
Slow, jerky shifting in fallback mode

P09A4.title: Gate Select Position Circuit B Low
P09A4.description: Set when the gate select signal on circuit B stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Likely causes are a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or an internal sensor short; with potentiometer sensors like the select position sensor in an Isuzu patent, an open signal wire often reads low too. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, nor whether B is a second track or another sensor. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P09A5 is the opposite fault, P09A2 the general circuit fault, P0906 and P09A8 the low faults of circuits A and C. If A and B are both low, look for a shared supply or ground.

causes.label: Signal wire of circuit B chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal short or broken wiper in the select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gear changes blocked or limited to a few gears
Transmission warning message in the instrument cluster

P09A5.title: Gate Select Position Circuit B High
P09A5.description: Indicates that the gate select signal on circuit B has stayed above its highest valid value for longer than allowed. Typical reasons are a short of the signal wire to the sensor supply or battery voltage, an open sensor ground, or a defective sensor. No manufacturer publishes how it uses this code or what circuit B physically is. An Aisin AI patent shows the consequence of losing select feedback: warning, request to stop, then a limp-home in first gear. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P09A4 is the low counterpart, P09A2 the general fault, P0907 and P09A9 the high faults of circuits A and C. A gearbox that can no longer confirm its gate restricts shifting.

causes.label: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Limp-home mode with very limited gear choice

P09A6.title: Gate Select Position Circuit C
P09A6.description: Electrical fault on a third gate select position signal (circuit C) that fits none of the more specific C codes. Public AMT designs show far fewer channels: Aisin AI and Isuzu use one select sensor, and a Mannesmann Sachs patent combines motor encoders with an extra neutral position sensor. What a third channel is in practice remains open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P09A7 to P09A9 are the plausibility, low and high faults of C; as with circuit B there is no intermittent variant. P0904 and P09A2 cover circuits A and B. Gear changes may be limited.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or wet connector at the select sensor or actuator unit
Damaged signal wire of circuit C in the gearbox harness
Faulty sensor supplying signal C
Faulty input stage for circuit C in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Delayed or missing gear changes
Vehicle reluctant to pull away

P09A7.title: Gate Select Position Circuit C Range/Performance
P09A7.description: Rationality fault on gate select circuit C: the value is electrically valid, yet it disagrees with the other select channels, the learned gate positions or the commanded movement. A Mannesmann Sachs patent shows why several select signals can exist: when one sensor fails, the remaining ones still allow controlled positioning before an emergency mode based on stored drive times takes over. No manufacturer documents this code or the role of circuit C publicly. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P09A6, P09A8 and P09A9 are electrical faults of C, P0905 and P09A3 the same check on A and B. The driver usually notices slower or restricted shifting.

causes.label: Drifting or worn sensor so signal C disagrees with the other channels
Select positions not relearned after repair work on the actuator or gearbox
Loose sensor mounting or magnet shifting the measured position
Contact resistance in the connector of circuit C

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slower or hesitant gear changes
Some gears no longer offered

P09A8.title: Gate Select Position Circuit C Low
P09A8.description: The module stores this code when the gate select signal on circuit C remains below its valid range for a calibrated time. Common triggers are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or an internal sensor fault; depending on the sensor type, a broken signal wire can read low as well. No manufacturer documents this code publicly or explains what circuit C measures. Patents from Isuzu and Aisin AI show the select sensor as the feedback the module needs to line up the right gate. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P09A9 is the high counterpart, P09A6 the general C fault, P0906 and P09A4 the low faults of A and B.

causes.label: Signal wire of circuit C shorted to ground
Sensor supply for circuit C missing or pulled down
Internal short in the sensor delivering signal C
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox holds one gear or drops to neutral
Transmission warning message in the instrument cluster

P09A9.title: Gate Select Position Circuit C High
P09A9.description: Logged when the gate select signal on circuit C sits above its highest plausible value for longer than a calibrated time. Usual suspects are a short to the sensor supply or battery voltage, an interrupted sensor ground, or a sensor with an internal fault. No manufacturer publicly documents this code, and the physical meaning of circuit C is not published either. An Aisin AI patent describes the fallback once select feedback is lost: warning, stop request and a limp-home in first gear. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P09A8 is the low counterpart, P09A6 the general C fault, P0907 and P09A5 the high faults of A and B. Shifting is usually curtailed.

causes.label: Signal wire of circuit C shorted to supply or battery voltage
Open or corroded sensor ground
Internal fault of the sensor delivering signal C
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Limp-home mode, often in a single low gear
Gear changes refused while driving
